review_text:
I’ve had this game in my library for a long time, and while I did love what I tried of it at the time, I never really quite got around to really playing it.  That was, until recently, and man was I missing out.  Shadow Tactics is a RTT stealth game that centers around a party of five unique characters, hired by the shogun to investigate the chaos forming in Edo Japan.

The cast is well-designed, making them unique both in-game and as characters, and the challenges presented will require all of their talents.  The overarching plot is fine, but it’s really the moment to moment gameplay and character-driven narratives that make it worth remembering.  The settings, setpieces, and music are also great and immersive.

I’ve always treated stealth games as a really big puzzle, breaking things down step by step to get to the end goal.  With such a varied cast, there are many ways to approach problems, supported by the variety of objectives presented within the game.  I definitely have opinions on what the “easiest” way to approach a level was, but I know what I did was just one of many.  The quicksave/load system also encourages that experimentation, making trial and error quick and painless.  It really is fundamentally strong overall.

At the time I bought it, I really didn’t know what I was missing out on.  It’s clear to me now that Mimimi Games is the king of RTT stealth, and now I’m hooked.  They really understood what made the genre good and put their own original spin on it.  They’ve got some new games coming out too, and I’m excited to see how things go!

review_text:
IMPORTANT NOTE: I actually liked the game A LOT, my negative review is solely due to to the fact that the DLC "Final Transmission" is actually the final chapter of the game, which is locked behind a paywall. I believe this type business practice in the gaming industry to be almost an scam from the developers publisher / parent company. No real game developer would support this type of behaviour, I greatly apologise to the Striking Distance team, but this is the only way I have to make my discontent public.

The actual review.

I know that the game bombed for a number of reasons, an I believe the main one being the high expectations for this game to be a spiritual successor from Dead Space. Glen Schofield and the team from Visceral Games hit the jackpot with Dead Space (my all time favorite survival horror game in the genre), but Lightning is unlikely to strike twice at the same place.

The influence from Dead Space is heavy here, but this is no spiritual successor but it is it's own game, and a very good one on that.

If you approach this game with the mind set of Dead Space, you will be unhappy with the results, but if you come with an open mind and take this game for what it is I believe you will really enjoy it.

I have two complaints for this game.

1- The dodging mechanic on it's current state was brilliantly implemented, but it could have been better specially when dealing with crowds. In it's current form, even with great situational awareness the dodging can be very frustrating, and there is no way to quickly turn around and/or maneuver your way out of the combat, regroup and have at it. The melee mechanic is a great addition to the genre that it's stuck on almost exclusively  in gun play, so it's a breath of fresh air in being able to bash my way out, but not having a broader set of evasion was complicated to put it politely.

2- This is one it's just me being really picky, but not allowing me to organize the inventory is really f***** up. A great deal of the game is inventory management and not being able to organize the inventory in a way that I have the items on a way that it's easy for me to glance on and know made me tired really fast.

Other than this two points, Callisto Protocol is an easy 8,5/10 for me!

review_text:
Can't believe I missed this gem until last week and really looking forward to whatever updates might come in future, although the game is pretty compelling as it stands and so far rock solid.
I like the style of using god-like powers to help various things along (I'm heavily using the grab option for example to kill off high HP enemies, help speed up buildings and focus my defensive minions against the enemy base), as opposed to the Rimworld style of micromanaging every detail of job/task/priority. I feel like I matter a lot more and can quickly influence outcomes. It might be because it's just a hard game, especially when those spawns get stronger and you fail to stop enough corruption from spreading, and having that rapid response grab ability is just a necessity. 
I have a couple of gripes, 1) the minions could path better, e.g. if there is wood next to a thing being built, pick it up instead of going all the way back to base to get a piece from storage and 2) don't stray into the corruption to hit a crypt unless its partially covered by light (fire) because that's insta-death. It means you have to be watching everything all the time, which is kind of hard (especially when you don't find the UI scaling option and can see only a limited portion of the map, yes, I'm an idiot). 
Having said both those negatives, and despite a lot of horrible minion deaths, I'm not bothered because it's my fault (I'm god after all and there are plenty of ways to prevent minions dying), it adds to the challenge, sometimes accidents happen and everything else about the game just feels so well put together and fun to play. I'm confident this game will remain in my top 5 best game list for a long long time to come. Hats off to a heroic dev, yes just one dev !!!

review_text:
TLDR: Better than the last one by a country mile, and managed to come out in less time (but not by much), it's basically just a really big walkaround, with enough dialogue stuffed in it to rival the Epilogue.  If you don't like long tedious branching pathways invariably clogged by wordswordswords, then I'd suggest at least avoid paying for it.  I backed this game eight years ago, before we knew what we were in for, don't make my mistake!  Hardcore fans only.

The second Act of Hiveswap (thankfully, mercifully) outdoes its predecessor in almost every respect, which is a huge relief.  The early minigame (singular) is more engaging and fun than all the rough and tedious minigames from the first game.  The soundtrack is improved greatly by being more Fox and less Roach, and every character is meticulously animated in their sprite's movement and expression, and I cannot praise this facet enough.  You're not buying the story, you're buying the characters.  I LOVED each of these characters, even though (and probably because) I never played any of the Friendsim spinoffs and only heartell of their exploits or flaws from other obsessed fangirls.  All of the background characters have animations too, from the paranoid to the relaxed or jovial!  Of all the little quirks and features, Zebruh's walk animation is definitely my favorite thing in the whole game, it's just... such a pleasure.  They'll probably be the only thing keeping you in the game.

Each of these alien characters is very charming, likable or... engaging at some level, and the game makes sure you spend as much time with each one as possible.  That's why half of the achievements require six hours of backtracking to undo a minor choice early on so a different particular character shows up later.  And they're all mutually exclusive.  Seriously.  You have to play through the whole 10-hour game a minimum of four times to get all the achievements.  Not even Black Mesa was this cruel!

People have complained about how there is no "dialogue backspace" button and it makes it difficult to remember or comprehend certain story elements if you weren't listening, but that adds to the realism and I greatly enjoyed it!  They don't just repeat the same things over and over like a robot, they'll say something else as if it were a real conversation and they're not gonna repeat themselves.  This also shows the sheer depth of the writing scale as each character has new things to say with each story beat!  Don't worry about missing info; if you want all the achievements in the game, you're going to be rereading the same dialogue several times anyway.

As for bugs, the only ones I encountered were cutscene glitches which served to heighten the atmosphere of terror in the later stages of the game involving... well I'd rather not say.  Let's just say it gets disturbing and the alien companion's fears are justified.  But I digress!  Act 1 was bug-ridden garbage, the bugs in Act 2 are minimal.  This is probably because they cut all the minigames, which was the worst part of Act 1 by a longshot.

As for the quality of the writing itself, it's still a far cry from Hussie's rapier wit, but it's not the Cohenist veganism either.  There's some preachy segments about classism or halfhearted sentiments about challenging the system through rap, but it doesn't go anywhere and wasn't nearly as heavy-handed as the Peta-esque nonsense from the last game that they thought passed as dialogue.  The dialogue in this game is a lot cleaner and less awkward, and does a great job handling large amounts of characters.  

It's everything it promised to be.  Either that, or my expectations got so low I forgot what I paid for.

review_text:
I have read some of the negative reviews and I'm a bit puzzled by them.  So a few things before we get started:

1 - you can adjust audio, movement and game play through the in game menu, you can mute npc or players, and yourself, change movement, change how weapons are loaded or held, change holsters, and many other options.
2 - the game is fun because you are playing with other people, might not be many maps but I promise each battle is different depending on the people you are with and it gets addictive pretty fast, try a more difficult setting with seasoned players and go for the more rare upgrade disks
3 - your weapons can be customized as you progress, you can also find weapons in many maps, door card keys open rooms with free weapons, floppy disks unlock weapon upgrades like scopes and magazines, the harvest you collect allows you to purchase unlocked weapons, upgrades and skins
4 - if you are dropping weapons, again the in game menu has options that will prevent it, change your settings
5 - if you are getting stuck, set movement to instant to disable the animations, its a known bug the devs are working on

There are very few VR games that are both co-op and fun, this is both of those things.  You can go it alone with AI or team up with all kinds of gamers.  The devs are aware of the bugs, but show me a VR game that does not have bugs.  At least this one is actually fun to play.

It's not a perfect game but I'm constantly drawn to it.  I recommend trying it and supporting it, more content will be added and the bugs will eventually be fixed.  Play it co-op, its like a party but you have to defend against zombies.  If you are having issues, ask a seasoned player in game for help, just another advantage of it being a co-op game.

review_text:
This game is VERY unique. I joined into this completely blind and I confess the first 30-40 minutes almost made me quit because the game told me so little what was that all about. Little by little I got to feel the world in this was so alive and full of personality. Story-wise this is top-notch. Graphics are below what you'd expect of a game from 2019. But the mechanics, the in-game market, the relationships built and commitments you decide to engage yourself in, and the different outcomes you can get are simply very impressive for a game that doesn't look capable of all that. The scenery and surroundings, the buildings in and out, they really exist and can be acessed (if their residents allow you to enter) and also they decay as time passes in-game, the whole city decays and changes, a feature that many new games try to do it but I've never seen it done so smoothly and having the player so swallowed by the story and the struggles to survive. This game is also known for being unforgiven, meaning that your actions will often have tougher and harder outcomes to deal with, and you will have to learn how to survive in this as you try to progress the story.

If you just want a relaxing or fun time, THIS IS NOT FOR YOU.

If you want a serious mature themed game filled with struggles to survive, bizarre unfolding events that can change according to your decisions, and that keeps pushing you to look for solutions while you deal with your morals at the same time, THIS IS FOR YOU.

review_text:
The Callisto Protocol is to Dead Space like Dark Souls is to Sekiro. 
If you've stepped in to The Callisto Protocol expecting a Dead Space successor, you're clearly mistaken. Yes, the game was created by the same head developer, and the game shows clear signs of inspiration from the Dead Space series. Gameplay-wise, it's gone from a dismemberment-focused shooter, to a bash-em-up melee, and this direction has clearly divided many of the Dead Space fans that the game was advertised to, but for those who welcome the new direction, will surely enjoy it.
When the game works, it works, graphics are stunning and sound design is excellent, with the dodge-and-smash gameplay mechanic being fun as hell, when it works...
The development team tried too hard to keep the game far from being a Dead Space 4, and the game was rushed to meet deadlines, and the game shows that, with heavy stuttering despite pre-loading shaders and inconsistent story-pacing, with the ending left as DLC.
At launch, this game was objectively unplayable, but with years of constant fixes, it's much more stable in comparison and is very enjoyable, and can now be recommended for others. 
All that being said, please buy the Deluxe Edition on sale ($17.54 AUD at time of review) should you decide to purchase the game. It's moronic to keep the base game at $87.95 AUD with cosmetics and extra story content locked behind a season pass for $43.95 AUD.

I love this game like an abusive spouse. 

It's is borderline busted. Your hand will get caught in geometry and it feels impossible to escape it. The holstering system is janky at best. About 70% of the time, when you reload your weapons before emptying your clip, your mags will fall straight to the ground even though you release the mag directly inside of your belt. 

The campaign is frustrating, sloppy and short, consisting of long stretches of the funkiest, most infuriating platforming sections you've ever seen, depending on unreliable mechanics like vaulting to climb on top of objects and ledges, and crouching to avoid a moving train that will probably hit you regardless of how low you get. 

Honestly guys... why so much platforming? You guys really thought the platforming in this wonky psychics sim was so fun it needed to be the highlight of this game? 

Still one of the best VR games on the market. That should tell you everything about what this market is like.

There isn't another game that has a better body implementation in VR, (Other than Boneworks.) Gun play shines as some of the most fun I've had in VR. Exploration is great, love the music, the world, and the meta storytelling. Lots of interesting secrets to find. Mod support is great, although there is still no in-game mod browser. 

TL:DR Buy Bonelab for free mods like Fusion, custom maps, guns and skins. Buy Boneworks if you want a fun, well thought out single player campaign. There's no good reason why this game costs more than Boneworks, a superior package in pretty much every way.

However the gameplay itself does not make me want to continue playing it, as it doesn't have this addicting feeling of doing another and another run.
Starting a new run does not feel like an exciting opportunity to craft or discover cool builds, more like being tossed into another empty island with some enemies sprinkled on it that you kill with the same weapons over and over and sometimes weird animations (like the musket boys who trace my dash with their shot).

The world and it's vibe are awesome, but the maps feel so empty with only a few objects being interactable like random ammo chests (who would randomly store Preyer ammo in their witch-dominated town?). After the intro sequence, I wanted to feel like I'm this elite mutant fighting on the frontlines of this holy war. kinda like a Black Templar of Warhammer 40k - but instead I was just a dude dashing through levels to farm some souls on samey enemies.

Also the music is great, but isn't nearly as present as I think it should be, as you barely notice it in battle.

Altogether everything except the actual runs is pretty good, but I'm mostly here for fun and fast gameplay - maybe that's my fault for excepting some kind of doom-souls-hades mix. 

Kudos for the optimization though, the game runs perfectly.

review_text:
Rise to Ruins is a fantastic town management god-sim tower defense game that can best be described as The Settlers vs. Dungeon Keeper. You play as a benevolent god of some kind that is trying to guide a group of people to a safe future in a world where the dead walk and hate humanity. They will attack in the night, and your villagers will need to be ready with walls, towers, golems, and gates. Your villagers will mostly build, repair, and arm these machines as well as build the necessary infrastructure to do so, as well as gathering their own food and water, and building their own shelter. You, of course, will tell them what to do.

It's a slow-moving game, but I love the relaxing music that plays in the daytime as well as the tense ominousness of night. If you need constant action, this is not for you, but if you ever wished that chill city-building games like Banished could come with a tower defense mod that throws zombies and ghosts at you every night, then this is definitely for you.

review_text:
UPDATED REVIEW (with old one below for transparency):
Seeing as how Steam has officially given the dreaded "14 months have passed" badge of shame, I think its about that time. The more I've come to understand the state this game is in through it's discord, in which I have lurked about 2 years now, things are not going well and the community will make your eyes roll into your head.
Sprinkled in between memes and echo chamber-esque circle jerks of moderators and longtime community members, there seemed to be genuine progress posted by the developer in the announcements channel of the official discord. Promising gameplay and seemingly fully functional mechanics related to movement, combat, enemies, ect. were being shown for the better part of a year. Much of it seemingly ready to build up to the "10 year anniversary" in September 2025. Myself and many others were expecting an announcement date for 1.0, at the very least. Instead, the dev released a short trailer showing a nostalgic look at an early build of the game, mixed with a short bit of footage from a slightly new intro sequence for the upcoming planned 1.0. It wasnt even posted here, on the official game page and steam community announcements.
The cherry on top of this baffling "announcement" was the dev saying they will soon be pulling the purchase option from the store page until 1.0 is done. 
I understand game development is hard, I understand it takes time, there are plenty of other things to do and people need to be patient. Holy moley though, this one has confused the absolute hell out of me. If you try to bring any sort of optimism about release coupled with questions about progress to the discord, be prepared to be met with disingenuous responses. If you suggest posting a potential release window or steam announcement so people are actually informed on the state of the game, be prepared to get told about how "risky" that is and similarly disregarded.
Brother, life is risky in general. If there really is that much more to do still then just get on it instead of taking a bunch of time making goofy jokes and non-committal, lukewarm posts about things being worked on.

In case any members see this and feel like responding, feel free to tell me I'm wrong below and prove my point more.
Looking forward to 1.0.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I never played the previous iterations of GTTOD, so I was confused when I saw the negative reviews saying the game was ruined with the change of the game becoming a roguelike. So take that into consideration I guess, but honestly what's here is so cool that I don't even care.

Some minor complaints first, then I'll get to the good stuff:
-The movement takes a bit of getting used to (especially wall running). I've fallen through the floor/environment at least twice in 5 hours. so that could use some work. Dont Expect Ultrakill levels of precision.
-Also, many of the guns feel like you don't have to be perfectly accurate to hit enemies. This can be a good and a bad thing I suppose, but it really threw me off at first, basically if an enemy is in your crosshairs, you'll hit em.

Thats about it for the negatives so far.

Past that, the MUSIC holy moley. So fitting and really pushes you to go insane-o mode.
The hub world is really neat, lots of practice tools to get your feet wet with how the game feels. 
Neon aesthetic and weapon design all look and feel pretty great, the roguelike elements are fun to shake things up every run and I'm enjoying the meta-progression. 
Overall, not sure why people are whining about this one. Definitely a hidden gem that deserves a higher % of reviews and I'm likely going to keep playing for probably another 80 hours if this one hooks me the way Roboquest did.

If you aren't a real serious gamer who loves being punished and abused by the game don't waste your money on this.

Now trying to do the hermit quest and the miller quest and they are bugged.  Oh, just so much of a pain in the a$$.
Latest grumble is if you finish a quest before going back to follow up, if possible with NPCs that gave tips or offered a reward you may not get it.  Latest quest to do this was the hermit quest. I stumbled upon the quest item and well, no more hermit, no talking with those who had provided tips and said come back and get a reward.  So the XP, coin and story are missed out on.

Oh yay, now my character does what he wants and then goes unresponsive to inputs...oh yeah, just so much f*cking fun.  The duels aren't even worth trying. review_text:
It is absolutely not a perfect game, there are small but infrequent bugs and the social/family aspects of the game are pretty bare bones, but it is a good game that I enjoy nonetheless, and keep in mind that this was made by only two developers. 

The artstyle is adorable and pleasing to look at. The music can be repetitive but it's relaxing to zone out to.

 The gameplay is good, there is a story but it's definitely not the most in depth and there is little to no reward for following/completing it. Where it really shines is the various randomized quests you can take on from the villagers. They always give you something to do, and you never know what kind of cool things you could get as a reward. Just be careful during selection because some quests are impossible to complete if they ask for something out of season, and you can't discard quests until they naturally expire on their own.

The aging system is fun, seeing the original NPCs experience different lives each playthrough is a cool touch, and it's fun to see how different your town looks year by year. Getting to play as your kids is pretty awesome too, but I do wish you could have the option to play as a child if your heir is still young when your main character dies. It feels weird to just suddenly age up to an adult when the kids born before you are still kids! Perhaps it could be an optional choice, for those who just want to move on and get their character married, but I would love to experience my character's childhood to feel immersed. Gameplay wouldn't have to change at all either, because you simply inherited the farm as your new job!

The difficulty is very customizable, you can remove aging, illness, minigames, and item decay to make your experience as stressful or peaceful as you want. All I really do is remove the fishing minigame because it's a lot of work for not a lot of reward. I also only take on one quest at a time because I get overwhelmed easily, but I've seen plenty of people with huge lists of quests to occupy themselves with if that's more your style!

Overall, there is room to improve, but the devs slowly continue to add updates and content as well as bug fixes, and I'm excited to see where things go from here! I would definitely recommend this to anyone who likes farming/life sims, and the actual Sims franchise as well!

review_text:
FIRST AND FOREMOST: NOT RECOMMENDED AT FULL PRICE, BUT RECOMMENDED AT 75% OFF.

I have absolutely no choice but to compare this game to it's ancestor Commando 2. Let's just say that it's a cheap version of that game. With C2 you had tremendous depth, an inventory system, characters that played drastically different, huge maps with a zoom out function that would let you get a real look at the whole map, real fleshed out buildings that you had to interact with, near infinite ways to approach a map. That's it on top of my head.

With this game, you get a watered down version of that. No inventory system, a dumbed down building system, no far zoom, smaller maps, few characters that play more or less the same. I guess that I'm happy that games are still produced in this genre, but I'm sad if that's supposed to be Commandos spiritual successor. Get it at 75% off, Idk what happened to the gaming industry, it feels like creators don't put in the work anymore. This game does not deserve the "overwhelmingly positive" tag.

I am a long time player with over 380 hours clocked. I started this game for the humor but fell in love with the community and although imperfect I could easily look past it and found myself lounging on rocks, exploring, chatting, and hunting for hours. I have gotten to know so many players and have even gained friends along the way. Getting excited to see each new animal and update, but with that being said I cannot sadly, recommend this game. 

For the reasons following: 
- [b]With every new update, one or more features break and they are fixed at slow pace if at all.[/b]
  - Ex. Crocodiles added -> Birds broke, they can no longer grab animals (food) a vital feature for their survival. It has been months with still no fix or word on them.
- [b]Rushes to push animals out with out fixing previous issues or animals.[/b] 
  - Animals being shoved out unpolished often with balancing issues and or broken features which they slightly band-aid but never fully fix, just enough to get by. This leads to over powered or under powered glitchy animals. It often feels like many things are not tested before they are released.
   - Ex. leopards have a climbing feature that was added many months ago but you will find yourself struggling to scale rocks and trees unless you hit things /just/ right. Terribly dangerous if you have predators chasing you. Crocodiles are over powered still, able to take down full elephants and hippos hitting for over 3k damage at times. 
- [b]Lion Favoritism[/b]
  - This game heavily leans towards lions as the favorites, they are terribly unbalanced and a few elders can easily take on full grown elephants, crocodiles, hippos, leopards, you name it. When we know that is not something even vaguely possible with out lions paying dearly in the wild. 
- [b]Playing as a Herbivore is not fun.[/b] 
  - This game makes playing as a herbivore absolutely miserable, they designed zebras and wildebeest to be practically made of glass even with moving your stats around. When they are able to deal some hearty damage in real life. You will not get that strong, powerful, herbivore feel in this game. Even as elephants, rhinos, and hippos...if you have a crocodile or two chasing you or a few lions you are typically toast as they pursue you to the end of the map.
- [b]Privately hosted servers with house rules made on the spot and often admins playing favorites.[/b]
  - If you are still determined to buy this, be prepared to have only one or two populated servers to pick from with rules you will not know with out joining their Discords. You will get scolded and dragged if you break one even if you are brand new more often than not. This often chases new players away who arrive, spawn in and explore and fight back when they are suddenly attacked not quite knowing the rules of engagement yet. Also be prepared for heavy favoritism as admins do their best to turn blind eyes or defend the regular favorites even if they break said rules and run to their aid when they claim you broke one. It is a very disheartening feeling as you try your best to explain your side but the favorite's voices are always louder leading to an unhealthy community as of late.

So overall, despite all the time I have poured into this game and the memories I have I cannot recommend it for these reasons. But I will always treasure the little memories I do hold with it from earlier days and hopes one day it will better but that is looking bleak.

review_text:
[b]An extremely story-driven JRPG about people playing an MMO, where the worst part about it is the actual game you're playing.[/b]
This consists of 3 HD remasters of the .hack//G.U. games released back in the mid-2000's, and a brand new 4th volume included in this bundle that gives this whole saga a real conclusion.

The story is probably great. It's hard for me to take a plot seriously though when most of everything that happens occurs in the video game within this game. The world outside of the MMO and general lore of this series as a whole is far more interesting and incredibly vast, where the timeline takes place in the futuristic years of the mid-2010's and a lot happens on the outside just because of an MMO.
I think they expected you to have played the previous .hack games and watched the prequel anime though, as they make loads & loads of references to both, and I didn't figure a lot of it out until I watched the backstory videos and searched things up myself.

Ironically, despite the game being about another video game, the gameplay itself is the absolute worst thing about this. It's tedious, repetitious, has loads of pointless mechanics, and so on.
As a JRPG, there's little thought needed into actually playing the game. There are elemental weaknesses, shield breaking, status prevention methods, and all that, but you can go through the whole thing using the same "mash A to kill thing" strategy over & over again while the more complicated-sounding stuff can be completely ignored altogether. The only thing you'll have to worry about is finding equipment with bigger numbers than what you're wearing, but even then you can still get through the story with equipment a hundred levels lower than you so long as your character's level is at the appropriate level for a monster/dungeon; even upgrading said equipment is pointless as stats barely get a boost at all and stronger equipment comes by fast.
The only enemies that can actually give you trouble are the late bosses of each game, but even then you can overcome them fast by doing a quick grind prior to gain a few levels.
I believe they're aware of how terrible the gameplay is in this since they added a "Cheat Mode" to every game that pretty much allows you to breeze through each volume and focus only on the story.

Its storytelling is also pretty obnoxious. Too many times, they want you to log out of the MMO and check your mail to progress the story. Other times they want you to go through a pointless dungeon and/or quest that has absolutely nothing to do with the plot itself, as if all it is is just to pad the time you play.

Each game lasts dozens of hours to go through first-hand if you play them "normally", except for the latest volume which only lasts a few hours and serves pretty much as the epilogue to the whole thing.
In the last volume, they still make you go through practically pointless dungeons even though you no longer need to do much or any leveling by that point, and the gameplay's pretty much the same as the first 3, which is dull.

If you really wanted to just go through the story, you're probably better off watching playthrough videos, or watch the .hack//G.U. Trilogy movie that covers the 3 games and maybe play the short 4th volume yourself.

It is a little reminiscent of Slay the Spire for me, in that it always provides a great challenge and I can find myself playing this easily for hours and hours on end. In addition to that they definitely take a page from the Slay the Spire devs with their weekly challenges (which came in a newer update after the game’s initial release). I love that, because sometimes I just want to play a run of this game with odd or interesting rules, verses playing the main/base game itself; for me, this breathes new life into this game. And the visuals—the visuals are very cute and mixed in with some of the humor in the game, just make it that much more enjoyable to play. I highly recommend picking up this game, and cannot wait to see what else the devs add to it!

review_text:
I want to like this game so bad, man. The movement is literally everything I want and more from a shooter and the roguelite stuff is fun. The problems start when you pair the two elements together. One thing is to have reloading weapons or limited ammo, but both? in a game where you're constantly jumping on and off walls, sliding, doing 180s to line up that perfect shot? Having to reload slows down the game, but running out of ammo and having to resort to the starting pistol (or worse, diving headfirst  into a group of enemies and spamming melee--which is actually pretty high damage and can outclass a lot of weapons if used right) just makes the pacing of combat feel weird. Having unlimited ammo would probably feel weird in a roguelite, and the roguelite stuff is core to the game (right now at least. I remember playing a demo years ago and IIRC the game didn't have those elements), so it's not like that's going away. This leaves the game in this perpetual swing state between the hypest fucking moments in gaming and the most frustrating interludes where you just wanna go back to shooting while flying from wall to wall but you can't because your character needs to reload two guns at once, or you've run out of bullets and need to melee 100 guys to get a meager amount of ammo back. Having to buy the guns is also grueling, since unless you spend all your permanent upgrade points on starting each level with extra shards (the game's currency), you're gonna have to kill a bunch of little dudes with the pistol and then go back to where you last saw one of the little slot machines where you get guns, which tend to spawn at the start of the level, forcing you to backtrack for them by the time you get the necessary shards. That's not to mention that you might get shotguns from said slots, and literally all the shotguns in this game suck. Again, you're flying from wall to wall or sliding at the speed of sound, so you're gonna be pretty far from the mobs you're shooting. Guess what kind of guns aren't effective at that range?
Idk. It feels like there's a lot of potential in this, and I wish all shooters had a movement system half as good as this, but the game also feels impossibly blind to its own intrinsic design issues. I hope the dev can find a way to make it all make sense, but as of now, things are pretty unfocused.

review_text:
Ok... So... Just Cause 4... Just Cause 4 Reloaded is... absolutely fine. That's it, fine. Not awful, not bad, not horrendous like some people say, it's just fine. When compared to JC2 or JC3, yeah, not good looks, but looking at it as it's own game, it's fine, even great at some fronts.

Just Cause 4 finally has a different story than "overthrow an authoritarian regime in Central America", also, finally some character development too, Rico is a bit more grumpy than expected, but still a good character. The story has... Something! They tried for once, it's no God of War but it gets the job done, and of course, ends on a cliffhanger. I will never forgive you if you don't give us a JC5 Avalanche >:(

Gameplay is better in every way imaginable (M/KB), some things were added, some removed, some changed (don't know who had the idea to auto-retract the tethers >.>), but overall, I still like it. Much easier to control Rico in the wingsuit and use all the gadgets. 
Gunfight is still the same as JC2 and JC3, and by that I mean that it still awful. Using the rifles feels like you are shooting stone statues with a healthbar and that's it. No impact animations, no blood wounds, no physics, no gore, once their health reaches zero, the stiff statues become a ragdoll, and that's it. 
Use explosive weapons or shotguns, believe me, much better.

Action is still awesome, destruction physics are the best of all JC games, the tornadoes ripping through the land and taking everything along with it is marvelous, I do wish we had more control of the weather effects tho, it's pretty complicated to control the Tornadoes for example. Ah yes, the turret sections are fun too.

The mission structure is... Strange, you have to release a few regions to unlock main missions, it's fine tho, can get tiresome but nothing extreme. I just played the main campaign, wasn't in the mood to 100% the game, I just released the regions and made the main missions, had a pretty decent time, but if you do all sides it will probably take forever and be boring.

Graphics are a mixed bag, the horizons looks beautiful, the explosion effects are among the best I have ever seen, the particles, fire, rain effects, all brilliant. As for the atmosphere, it has a darker tone to it, specially when compared to JC3, it's taste, I like it but I get those who enjoy a more vibrant experience. As for the bad, man, the lightning and texture work of the cutscenes are HORRENDOUS, my god, what happened there? Literal PS1 textures, sometimes the hair glitches, Sheldon looked like he had metal hair and beard on some cutscenes, the cutscenes are waaaay too dark and low res (literally 480p), I don't know why they did it, the in-game cutscenes are MUCH better. Last, of course, the ocean, yea the water is strange man, while it looks good at night with winds, during the day it looks like paper. Awful.

The performance is also fine for me, no framedrops at all, not even in tornadoes, the FPS is completely stable, much better performance than JC3 in all possible fronts and I had a single crash while playing and reproducing a stream on my second monitor. The only stutters I had was when I completed a leaderboard challenge, but once I disabled those in the menu, no more stutters.

As an old time fan that played all JC games (Really old, JC1 on PS2 was fire), I actually like it. Not the best Just Cause, but not the atrocity people make it. 
I would give it mixed rating, but since I like it more than dislike it. Soft recommended.

review_text:
Dead by Daylight - a name-based breakdown

[b]Dead[/b]
You play in one of two teams (yes, a solo team is still a team), either trying to do the dead to someone or avoiding becoming the dead.
As the killer, it is your job to find people, run in circles of varying radii while dodging pallets thrown at you for at least 10 minutes, attack survivors with often questionable hit registration, and scramble to find a hook in proximity. Rinse and repeat thrice per survivor.
You also get a large cast of characters with increasingly broken and more abundant abilities and perks (scaling with in-game and IRL money cost, of course).
As a survivor, your job is one of: Holding Mouse Button 1 for an eternity and occasionally tapping space, running in circles of varying radii while dodging the killer, dropping pallets and jumping through windows, and enjoying the scenery while [i]hanging around[/i].

[b]by[/b]
By choosing to play this of your own free will, you prove that you are masochistic.
As the killer, the survivors always find some random junk scattered by a tornado to hide behind, and as a survivor, the killer is always slightly* faster than you.
If you are planning to play a killer with projectile or ranged attacks, dont't. Hitboxes in this game have been proven to protrude into the 7th dimension, especially those that don't look that way.
Conversely, survivors have been known to have been hit by attacks through solid objects.
Really shows how our understanding of physics breaks down beyond the third spatial dimension.
Also remember to pray to RNGsus before running through shrubbery, as it might be of the 'solid' genus despite sharing the phenotype of their 'transparent' siblings.
It's also funny how there are never any windows or pallets while you are being chased. Well, back to admiring the level geometry.

The performance is also abysmal. Lowering the graphics settings barely makes a difference, as the game is consistently gobbling up 80-100% of my CPU even while not much or even nothing is happening (e.g. game lobby, transition screens).
Depending on the map, it turns into a PowerPoint presentation as soon as at least one other player is on screen for no discernable reason.
On a positive note, I no longer have to change settings every time I boot up the game, so a big round of applause.

[b]Daylight[/b]
This game is anti-fun regardless of which team you play on, regardless of you win or lose. Good games where neither team is completely steamrolled are few and far between.
It seems like you are placed in the timeout box after dominating too many matches in a row and are free to return after serving your sentence. If that's your thing, good for you, but that ain't it, chief.

Specifically for 2V8 (the only theoretically redeemable mode**) the killer queues are a joke. You usually wait 30+ minutes for a match, and too often just so that the survivors can complete the 'DBD All 8 Generators' 100% glitchless speedrun in 2m 57s.
How is this possible when there is a 5-digit player count at all times? The introduction of 'Survive While You Wait' has done precisely nothing and the priority queue got ditched after one iteration of this game mode for reasons I don't care enough to look up.
At least you may partake in fun activities such as: Holding Mouse Button 1 (but more often because no one else is doing it), getting nothing done while being permanently cornered by 2 killers, and getting ignored by up to 7 players while in a cage collecting hook states (what do you mean that's not the objective???).

I'm being held here against my will by a so called 'friend' who's only into these kinds of games. Please help.

* Top speeds of Mach 3 have been registered.
** Objective fact.

review_text:
Overall Score: 5/10
My advice: Only get it if you're really into 80's style movies and need something to crave a Far Cry itch until 4.
Genre: Action Adventure FPS, sandbox RPG.

Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon puts me in a difficult position. I loved Far Cry 3, and thought the creative direction to incorporate cheesy 80's-style humor with retro gaming was a neat take. But like... when you're playing a game, and you find yourself having to purposefully push yourself to keep playing it? That's a bad sign.

I'd give a plot synopsis, but really, there's not much more to it then "you're a badass cyborg on an island killing pretty much everything while you save the world for the USA." If the humor the game uses were enough to make up for the flat plot, this might be exclusable, but there were countless groaners that really fit the genre... too well. Guys, there's a reason we don't right corny as hell plots like this anymore.

Alright, so the story is flat and schlocky, how about the gameplay? Well, it's basically just Far Cry 3, except... detached. You've got maybe 6 hours in the core game, 16ish overall if you get all the collectables. They didn't add much new until really the end of the game, and really, half of what was so fun about Far Cry 3 was you ascended your character from weak chump to badass over the course of the game, discovering new skills and abilities. Here, you just start out a badass becoming a bigger badass, fighting hordes and hordes of bland, faceless enemies... It just kind of became boring. Vast murder and tons of explosions became boring. That's half the selling point of your game!

This game is so much more fun than the premise implies. Very much a "just one more round" game with levels of addiction I haven't experienced in a while. The gameplay is incredibly fun and addictive and when you hit the perfect shot, it feels euphoric. You can definitely draw comparisons to Rocket League, but this game still fills a unique role in car based sports games. Playing against your best time and trying to improve your technique feels really satisfying and winning or losing always comes down to your own decisions compared to a team based game like Rocket League. I've only had the game for a couple days and I can't stop playing. 

There are some rough spots in the game that need ironing out and some odd to downright frustrating interactions. That being said, I imagine that will be fixed with time, and the complaints are mostly minor, or involve the occasional head scratching moments where you ask yourself "did that really just happen?" One of the more memorable frustrations for me and my friends is how the game seemingly randomly will switch ball cam on or off during a set. It's frustrating, but not game breaking. Little things like this make you realize the game needs a bit more polish, but with the package it's currently offering, it's hard to complain too much.

Absolutely worth your time whether queuing solo or with friends. Grab it and don't look back. Just make sure you clear your schedule for the foreseeable future.

review_text:
Definitely one of the greater colony sims, but the game fails where most others do... no win conditions. Now before you lose your mind, I understand the concept of "endless" content, but this game specifically is capable of having win conditions with how each level can interact with one another. In its current state, you barely get to make use of the world map because you just get wiped on the first level. Each level is designed to go on forever, the "endgame" of each level is essentially a stalemate until the enemy inevitably out-scales you.

Instead, the earlier levels should be "beatable", meaning you can completely wipe out the enemy and have the map to yourself. The cleared maps would then be exclusively used as logistic bases to help fund your "front line" bases. As you advance through the world map, the enemy becomes a little more aggressive and expands a bit faster. Once you get to the last couple maps, the enemy starts to behave like it does now, where it essentially scales infinitely until you get wiped.

review_text:
Would like to give a positive review, but in it's current state, the game is a bit awkward.

On one hand, it looks really good, and the gunplay is incredibly good, but on the other, the difficulty spikes way high as you increase your gnosis... which is needed to progress. This is especially so when you have hordes of enemies pounce on you, others hitting you with ranged attacks, reducing your stamina, blinding you, setting you on fire, freezing you, electrocuting you, poisoning you, and essentially locking you into a no win situation. Add onto that the calamities that can suddenly appear out of nowhere if you do something wrong too many times while fighting hordes of enemies, and suddenly there is also a sanity mechanic. This is really bad when you are in the middle of a hectic fight and then you hear bells tolling. Oh and did I mention how you can have to fight very spongy hordes of enemies? You get a group of blunderbussers, grenadiers, and swordsmen and you are going to have a very bad day, any day of the week.

Not to mention that a lot of items don't seem to have a use right now. Black salt seems to be the one that comes to mind for me. But I know there are others. They'll probably have a use later, but for now, I would rather have something useful drop.

Weapons also have to be pretty close range to be effective. You will see them doing like 1 to 4 damage unless you get right up in the enemy faces. Which makes the only really good weapons the two shotguns the game has. The rest just feel like a squirt gun against the big armor clad brutes, that you will start to see tons of.

Right now, the game starts off pretty fun, but that fun wears off pretty quick by the time you get to the third area. By that point, enemies are so tanky, elites everywhere, tons of elemental damage thrown at you, lots of knockback, loss of max stamina from being hit, and quickly running out of ammo, and calamities constantly. It just gets way too punishing way too quickly.

Will keep an eye on it, but for now, I can't really recommend it. Are much more balanced fps games available.

This game makes me sad.  It's a classic story of "so much potential."  You basically play as a little devil-spawn kid (ala "The Omen") and run around the house plotting and executing the murders of various occupants in your house without getting caught.

The gameplay isn't bad, but it takes far too long to figure out what your objective is and where the things you need to achieve it are.  It would be a lot more fun if you could wander around exploring and gathering and then choose an execution method based on your inventory, rather than having to find the items for the single available method.

The other problem I had with this game was that it has far too many cutscenes which last for too long and happen too often.  It interrupts the gameplay.  At one point, you have to sneak out of your room to get some rat poison.  You have to sneak around without being noticed, which is actually a good deal of fun.  So I picked up the rat poison and expected to have to sneak back, but instead there was a cutscene that had me waking up the next morning.  One of the best parts of the old Thief game was trying to get back out after you've accomplished your goals.  No such "extra drama" here.  Just do your task and watch the next cutscene.

I was very happy I was able to give this game a try, but I can't say I recommend it.  It's just too frustrating, the voice acting is poor, the characters are either unbelievably mean or oblivious, your actions are too limited, and worst of all, the story isn't compelling.

Pretty good at what it's trying to do, but definitely not for everyone.

The game sets itself apart from most platformers with a veneer of player hostility in most of its design elements--weapons attack slowly, many weapons are single use, your dodge roll is clumsy, enemies deal brutal damage with quick attacks, HP and MP aren't refilled for free anywhere, etc.

However, it's kind of a smokescreen. Healing items are showered on you as you go, the AI is braindead, and many of the items are gamebreaking (including items that grant infinite free healing/MP refills, negate all traps/bad terrain, and infinite use ranged weapons).

Fortunately, none of that stops it from FEELING like you're triumphing over stacked odds and an unfair game. It's just hostile enough to feel good finding and using the stuff that's broken. You will have to proceed slowly and use your brain, but it's not actually that difficult except a few spots.

Other stuff: Visuals are quite good with great monster design and great animations. Enemy design+variety is pretty good. Boss design is hit-or-miss. Despite looking like a metroidvania basically none of the stuff you gain are used for exploration or movement.

review_text:
Classic case of a game that hasn't aged well. At all.

Perhaps I'm not the core demographic for physic puzzle games, but I distinctly remember finding games like Angry Birds or Cut the Rope more fun than this title.

The music is fine, graphics cartoonishly pleasing, and gameplay concept simple and effective. However, my main gripes come from the culmination of lackluster features that nearly all titles have nowadays, including recent puzzle games.

- Lack of music/volume/sfx menu 
- Inconsistency of move undo-ing for levels (It's there sometimes, not others, and often doesn't work the way it should)
- Screen is WAY too zoomed in, with no settings to change the window resolution
- The water physics are simply .... indescribable (It's near impossible to tell what's caused by your cursor or the objects themselves)
- Selecting goo balls that constantly move around make it easy for you to grab one you didn't intend, or worse, one that kept your structure up 
- Can't retry a level even if you complete the level unintentionally (OCD Achievement Hunters beware)
- Goo structures fall over each other in layers (Doens't make any sense to me why a structure is able to hang from itself)

[b] (Even though things like sound and screen resolution can be easily fixed with some file and mixer changes, it simply didn't improve the more apparent frustrations I had in the gameplay. So moreso, just a little insult to injury.)[/b]

Call me petty or downright stupid, but playing the same level over and over left me more frustrated than amused due to points such as these. [u]I'll appreciate the pioneering this game had done around a decade ago, but that doesn't mean it's the pinnacle iteration of puzzle games. I'd say it's best to leave the past behind on this one.[/u]

Old Review:

Although early access, EHM:EA is a very polished management simulation. If you enjoy hockey, or any sports gm games, you owe it yourself to pick this game up. 


From Version 15.0.1b (first early access version) here are some of my findings on the game:

Pro's: 
- Has nearly all the features from the EHM 2007, meaning it already is the deepest hockey sim available.
- Nice new touches like players bio information talking about players close friends on the team.
- Nice tactical improvements like individual strategies for players
-Tactical improvements for lines including choosing who would be the playmaker on the line.
- Free Agency is much more realistic. Don't expect to always build your teams on July 1st, UFA's want money and term just ilke in real life.
-Position's of players are more in-depth, including their roles like defensive defenseman, stay-at-home defensemen, 2-way forward, skilled forward, quick forward. This adds to the fun of building cohesive forward units.
-Tons of international tournaments, take control of your favorite national team and try to build a team to bring glory to your country.
-The in game match view has been improved and is very enjoyable watching your team battle it out.


Con's:
- Interface and menus are very similar to EHM 2007 so it is missing some more modern interface options.
- Resolution needs to be improved for modern pc's
- Scoring has to be balanced a bit more to 2015 scoring levels (its a bit too high at least in NHL games).
- Missing leagues like the Swiss leagues, Russian MHL, and British Hockey leagues from 2007 version.
- Coaches and GMs get fired a little more than in the real world.

There are a few issues like the small window the game runs in and the interface definitely needs some modern touches, but the rest of the cons are minor. The positives far outweigh the negatives with this release. Please do yourself a favor and buy this game if you enjoy the sport of hockey and have ever wanted to build your dream team or test your management skill in the lower leagues and build a legendary story as you climb the ranks to finally leading your national team to world glory.

review_text:
Scorn is a gory, alien body horror first person puzzle game heavily inspired by HR Giger's art.

Even though HR Giger is my favorite artist and this game seems to be tailor made for me, there is still no getting around it: Scorn is a BAD game. The TLDR is that the art is good, even great at times, but the gameplay is frustrating and mediocre, and the story telling muddled and confused, all of it often working against the whole.

The primary reason why I cannot recommend Scorn is that you spend a lot of time confused and lost, but not in a good way. While it could be fun to explore strange alien architecture, you instead usually hunt around the sprawling levels looking for the next interact-able object. You are looking for the video game piece to progress so you aren't looking at the pretty and detailed scenery. Because everything is so alien, the gameplay trains you to find things you can walk up to just see if the little interact-ability circle pops up. Not only is this boring and frustrating, it also makes you actively miss all that surrounds you. 

The game is really, really bad at telling you what it wants you to do to the point where I believe its a deliberate design decision. Branching paths, things circling back on themselves, events that seem nonsensical... it all makes you wonder what you are actually supposed to do. I think the idea was to force players to spend more time around the lush environments, but since I am running around with the purpose of progressing and the environments are NOT linked to that progress, you don't actually end up looking at it. I started the game taking my time, admiring the strange and grotesque artwork, but once I started encountering puzzles and play elements, I spent less and less time looking at the art. 

And it is art. The one thing this game has going for it, is of course the Gigeresque creatures and levels. And they are gorgeous. Brutal, sickening, yet sometimes alluring. And above all else, alien. Though of course the alien design doesn't help the gameplay at all because you can't identify what anything is really supposed to do. Its beautiful but not functional in a game.

That is the crux of the problem. The gameplay is actively bad and, on top of that, draws you away from the art, and the art doesn't help the gameplay at all either. And the isolated parts, like the puzzles and combat, are really simple and not much fun. I want to make clear, that especially for a game like this, it does not HAVE to be fun, it can bring something else to the table... but I do not think it does bring anything else to the table.

Also, just to make sure it is said, there is not much of a "story" here. There is no dialogue or text, but you could still tell a story through environmental storytelling. But Scorn somehow manages to flub this too. Things do happen but they don't really make sense. You are in a crumbling, seemingly forgotten facility. One of the first events encases you in some ooze, and then the facility is even more crumbling and more forgotten? Not sure what the takeaway is supposed to be. Which would be fine if there was some sort of emotional takeaway, but the game doesn't have a deft hand there either. Your character goes through some painful scenes, being horribly injected and the like, but its impossible to relate to your character so all those scenes fall flat. Your character takes punishment far beyond what a human could survive and continually does things no human would do or even think to do. Encounter a strange alien polyp device? Yeah, inject its fluid straight into my wrist, sure, why not. So all those scenes where our character takes a moment to look at the "strange" gun they just picked up don't work, because the things they treat as strange are no more strange than the things they treat as normal. Pulling out a tentacled umbilical chord really loses its punch when I both do not know how painful it is or if its even weird for the character. And because the facility is in disrepair and overgrown with strange alien stuff, but also some of the strange alien stuff is part of the machinery, its often impossible to tell what is a sign of decay, what is functioning as its supposed to, or what is supposed to be an invasive foreign entity. We have alien things interacting with alien things in alien ways, with not nearly enough context to get anything out of it.

Scorn is one of those interesting failures of a game where it is a little fun to pull at the strings and try to figure out why its a failure. I could write more about this game, even kind of want to. But I tell you what I do not want to do. Play more Scorn.

review_text:
This game takes on the appearance of a 2003 game, but that is very much a design choice made out of love, not to cut corners. The levels are low-poly, but very detailed, well-designed, fun to traverse. The movement tech is smooth and is easy to pick up with a high skill ceiling. I really liked collecting all the achievements for getting super high combos in every level, because you really have to know the level and plan a good path. That's when you realize that every little combo you found before can be linked together if you just play it right.

There's lots of small quality of life things too, that I didn't even think about until I tried to play Jet Set Radio for a bit. The ability to switch characters at any dance spot. The freedom to place your favorite graffiti anywhere. The convenient controls for the phone, making it possible to switch music during a combo.

That's already plenty reason to love this game and I didn't even mention the soundtrack yet.

Erm I'm getting a refund on this one. A whole lot of nothing from Bloober this round. Refund! I do not recommend spending $60 on this game.

review_text:
Yeah, it's fun. And makes a great early impression.

But after a bunch of soft-locks, chasing the 1000th guy around a tiny rock because he wants to play hide and seek, watching swordsmen glitch in every possible way, etc, I find I'm not having any fun.

The guns are cool. The spells are cool. The builds are cool. But the moment to moment gameplay fizzles for me. In this game with no real melee options baddies are constantly spawning directly behind you. Playing with a controller is a hassle just because you need to turn 180 so often.

Also, this game is so mini-map dependent, it's crazy. It's one of those games where you end up looking at your mini map more than anything, and without the mini-map on you'll constantly be stabbed in the back and miss every chest. I literally just watch the mini-map during boss fights, or any major incursion. There's so many graphical effects going you can't make heads or tails of the action anyway. So I just look at my mini-map, have the red dots and spray and pray.

I die a lot too, and it never feels good. Falling instantly kills you, even if you're supposed to have one free death. You get knocked off a cliff by enemies. One of your own weapons will often kill by knocking you backward, making it just unusable.

Spells are another frustration, if my spell cooldown doesn't come back I'm just dead. The timer is a lie and it only lowers the cooldown on enemy kills. I'll be stuck in a tense fight hoping the 1/100th of a cooldown passes and I can cast an important spell. It never does. It never will.

If I have to reload in a bad spot, I'm dead. Getting trapped in melee happens a lot. Leading to you often having to just sprint for open air before risking a fight, even with basic enemies. Shotguns are terrible in this game.

If a bunch of invincible swordsmen jump on me from a cursed chest, I'm dead. The curse chest that makes only one enemy vulnerable at one time is one the most tilting things ever. Because of the enemy's love of hiding behind small rocks.

Losing everything on death sucks. Yeah, I'm not super familiar with this genre but, regardless, it sucks. It makes me just want to put the game down when I die, not do another run. And you don't even get the loot you had back when you recover your body. Wow. Great idea.

Just as an aside, people don't really get Dark Souls do they? The secret of the games is that they aren't actually hard and that you never ever actually lose progress, just a handful of souls on death, which are always easily replaced, or you get the back from your blood pool.

Games like Witchfire, where you lose all progress on death, are not soulslikes. They're stupid. And frustrating. And when From Software made all the great strides forward in game designs these guys didn't pick up a clue.  Why you don't get the stuff you dropped on death is beyond me.

Also, if you get softlocked in the game you can't kill yourself, so you have to quit and literally lose all progress, (weapon kills, everything) Dark Souls also thought of the solution to this a long time ago.

 I keep finding more and more stuff that's just a struggle. And then I'm struggling to just have fun playing the game, which is what video games are for? Right?

This game is too much work. Maybe they'll fix it.

Also, I posted all this stuff in the forum but I don't think the devs read it. So maybe this'll help.

Yadda yadda yadda, I think this game will be a definite thumbs up when it reaches 1.0. Right now it's still baking.

review_text:
Gonna write this in english because i want the devs to be able to easily read it, but beware it's not my first language.

I really love this game, been playing it everyday since i bought it, but i had already played it in an earlier build (the game only had 2 maps then). This game is hard and unforgiving most of the time so i'm gonna do a list of things that annoy me. Please don't feel like i'm hating on the game, it's cool af, i just wish some things where better.

 
Hermitorium: I will never understand why this place must be so large. I mean it's a mild annoyance, but having to run around the place looking for the merchant or having to go downstairs everytime i want to check the gnosis progress gets annoying with time. Also are there plans to make the training room more useful? The test dummy dies too fast, it only serves to check how much damage your weapon is doing and the magic colldown doesn't reset so theres not much to test there.

Overall design: When i first saw the teaser for this game 7 years ago i got a huge Darkwatch vibe from it (trashy Capcom fps from 2005), i thought it would be super goth and wicked looking but the goth aspect is very dilluted in my opinion. Like i reach Velmorn and find a secret sniper there, the sniper has a scope with a cross in the middle surrounded by rose thorn looking stuff, but the actual weapon has a blue and red paintjob mixed with a brown wood funiture... Sorry to whoever made it, but it doesn't fit well to the setting and that goes to the vast majority of the weapons. Ok, i'm fine with hailstorm having a snowflake for a crosshair, but does it have to look like it came from santa's arsenal? The only weapons i have that really fit the game for me are Nemesis, Striga, Hunger, Psychopomp and Koschei. Also i know this is a huge nitpick, but when you shoot striga and you see that mundane, simple wooden stake magically materializing inside the barrel it's kinda funny.

Builds: I'm overall fine with it, but i think the Chronoclast should be removed. Yeah i see it's like elden ring or ds3 and you need a consumable to reset your points, but this is an extraction roguelike, not a soulslike. If i have to select an incense, choose and upgrade my weapons and magic before a run, why are you limiting my ability to build the character before tackling a spcific boss? It's probably not happening, but what if the whole level system was removed and the stat buffs came from the chosen fallen prayer? i got that idea from first berzerker khazan and to me it makes much more sense since the game is a roguelike. You find the mask shards, upgrade the fallen prayers with witchfire and each prayer has a different set of buffs focused in stuff like magic casting, weapons, meelee, etc. I'm also gonna add that the most OP builds for this game involve the Arsenal atribute 99% of the time and even if you build for witchery you'll still need good weapon handling and ammo reserves because of the cooldown system. Yeah leveling witchery reduces spell cooldown but to me the cooldown for spells is kinda unnecessary and could be substituted by a mana bar. Every time you kill an enemy the witchfire that comes to you would recharge a portion of the mana, enabling you to cast more often. I don't think any of this will be changed because the everything would have to be rebalanced, but it would be so much cooler and would make the builds completely chage the playstyle depending on what you choose.

Cruelty: My final complaint will be towards the abusing nature of certain parts of the game. There are moments in which the game betrays your expectations and makes it super easy, but othes in which you are obliterated for absolutelly no reason. The familiar from iron gate for example, i killed that sucker almost hitless in my first try with 8 crossbow shots and Echo spamming, but for some reason the path for the optional miniboss from Scarlet coast has poison flowers in the ground that take too much time to disarm, a ton of enemies shielded by hard to destroy efigies and like if that wasn't enough theres mines that deal heavy damage at the end of the tunnel, all that for a pretty mid, easy miniboss at the end and you can even disarm all the poison flowers in the arena before entering... Theres tons more like when the game accidentaly groups 3 enemy clusters in one spot and it becomes almost impossible to avoid wasting all your elixirs and ammo, the ammount of enemies you have to kill for each encounter and the ammo you have to spare is stupid sometimes, enemies should drop ammo more often! OH and what about the wailing tower?? You expect me to run around the island of the damned everytime so i can get strong before entering the tower just to recieve TERRIBLE debuffs, waste all my resources and have to fight a super hard boss, all for what? a machine pistol and some profecies... Sorry that is SH*T, theres no nice way of putting it. The tower's floors are hard, the debuffs are way too bad, enemies are annoying, numerous and the reward is weak.

Final thoughts: i like and recommend this game, but the direction some things took are down right bad. That doesn't mean i'm not playing when 1.0 is out as i said i love it ever since i saw the first teaser, but to me it could be better in simple ways that i'm sure the devs are capable of making. My only true request? Please add different weapon skins and make it so i can change the skins at the gunroom. Doesn't matter if they're free or require stuff to unlock them, just make it goth and spiky and i'll be happy.

It's not often I drop a positive review for a game, and then change it to negative in hindsight (except that one tower defense game but we do not speak it's name here), but here we are.

The game is fun at first, like I got a good 20 hours of fun from it and if you think that's enough for you, go right ahead, you'll get your money back. My issue is that once you know how the game ticks, it's EXTREMELY easy to beat it. So much so that even the secret hard mode the stand-in of the dev says "this mode was too hard but this is my true vision B)" is also stupidly easy.

So what do you do once the main game is completely trivialized? PvP. And nothing BUT PvP. And even better? PvP against people who religiously play the game and try to exploit every single stat or line of code possible so they can maximize their side so they're quite literally unkillable, turning the battle into a war of attrition until you eventually die.

This is your life now. You HAVE to participate in it because the base game's difficulty DOES NOT go up anymore than the directors cut. I personally signed up to play an army builder and fight NPC battles, not fight "Xx_DespotL0v3r69_xX"'s unbeatable army of anime girls.

I actually REALLY enjoyed the game back when I didn't fully understand it, when I was learning the ropes and getting a little closer to winning each time, but now that I've learned the rules, I can't un-learn them, and at the end of run I do I gotta draft my ass up to the PvP Pit and watch my guys get clobbered by #26 on the leaderboard of Despot's Stinkiest.

Again, if 20 hours is a good time sink for you, go straight ahead because the game is good for those 20 hours. But once those 20 hours are up, you're gonna be just like me. In the pits.

review_text:
This game was beyond disappointing, not just as a so-called new high for RPGs but also as a necessary sequel. I am completely baffled by the praise this game has received this year, and I almost feel lied to by critics and the public audience. In nearly all fronts I see this game as a small to large downgrade from its predecessor. Historical accuracy is given less importance, instead the game is “Marvelfied” with all these moronic one dimensional quippy characters with their catch phrases and lazy contrived conflicts. Such as getting too drunk so the enemy gets the jump on the heroes (happens multiple times). Even most of the soundtrack sounds far more fitting in the basic whimsy fantasy adventure game than in the rich historic countryside of Bohemia, especially compared to the first game. Gone is player choice or agency in the main quest (there are only TWO actual decisions in the whole main story wtf), this game is far far far more railroaded, everything plays out the same no matter what. Even the first game had freedom, like the Monastery quest, there was so so much player freedom and it felt like such an engaging quest to do. Instead we’re left with action-cutscene-action-walk and talk-action- cutscene, cause nothing's more immersive than following waypoints and orders right? And that would be fine if the plot or gameplay was great but it's far from that, it’s supposed to be a role playing game but you’re allowed only one role. Henry is an emotionally weak pansy who lets everyone tell him what to do, and you have no way of expressing yourself through him notably in the main quest. Characters will criticize and lecture you constantly, feels more like the writers of this game demand you to feel and act a certain way for their game to work. Combat sucks, you all should know that, waiting to master strike all game is lame and swords are the only viable weapon.

The map and graphics are beautiful, kuttenberg especially should be praised, too bad there's not a whole lot to engage with in it. I personally like the artwork of the map better in KCD1 but that’s completely subjective. 

Apparently I am almost alone in this opinion, I should be glad that so many people can enjoy it but I couldn’t enjoy this game past the 2nd act for everything listed above. I don’t believe it’s horrible, I just think from what was lacking in KCD1 that this game was gonna be it. Unfortunately it seems Warhorse went more in the consumer friendly direction and made a far more cliche action adventure game, than a modern classic of role playing. My frustration is just very deeply rooted in how much I enjoyed the first game and how excited I was to see their vision realized. But it seems they went the easier route, and made a safe and easy to digest experience. 

P.S. My thoughts aren’t fully expressed, I have so many more things to say especially when it comes to giving examples but I don’t want to overwrite, cheers to those who read.

This is the best game I have played in a long time. Finally a developer who creates a new IP that's worth playing in the sci-fi horror genre. Comparisons with Dead Space are inevitable but for me no matter how much I like Dead Space, i like Cronos: The New Dawn more. The atmosphere and graphics are amazing. The controls and weapons are great. The enemy's are very good and have a nice mechanism to create a sense of urgency to kill them and dispose of them. In the gaming landscape these days almost everything has been done before, so it's getting hard to figure out something new. Cronos blends the best from before in a new package and I applaud Bloober for that. Bloober has become one of my favorite developers. Guys and girls, buy this game. Don't wait or beg EA for a new entry or remake of Dead Space. There is a new sci-fi horror king. Such is our calling.

Edit: 9 hours in, GOTY.
