review_text:
[quote]“The real voyage of discovery consists not in seeking new landscapes, but in having new eyes.” 
― Marcel Proust[/quote]

In one word, [i]Samorost 2[/i] is a “voyage”.

[h1]Foreword[/h1]
I highly recommend trying out the original [i]Samorost[/i] before purchasing this installment. Available for free on the Amanita Design website, it's a fine point of reference to experience Amanita's style, and whether or not you'll appreciate it.

[h1]The premise[/h1]
[i]Samorost 2[/i] is an excellent -- albeit short -- sequel to the first installment of the series. The conflict starts when your cute dog gets stolen by creatures of vile intent, and you set after them to retrieve your loyal boy. From then on, you'll encounter obstacles and puzzles in the form of, among other things, bug-eating creatures, flying seals (?) and even wild dandelions.

[h1]Where it excels[/h1]
As it is the trademark of every Amanita Design game, when it comes to sound and visual effects [i]Samorost 2[/i] leaves nothing to be desired, and paired with intuitive puzzles and a delightful story, it is able to tell its tale in a smooth ride that allows its players to drink in its gorgeous scenery and poignant character design.

[h1]Where it falls short[/h1]
Sadly, [i]Samorost 2[/i] feels just a little bit too short. The game can be completed in roughly 1 hour, making one wish for more, despite the rounded conclusion.

To add to that, sometimes it is difficult to tell which elements are interactive, so some become harder not due to their design, but due to the fact that oftentimes their elements need to be, first and foremost, visually hunted down. This is an issue that Amanita has most certainly overcome in their latest titles, but which [i]Samorost 2[/i] falls prey to one too many times.

Lastly, the very last puzzle [spoiler](taxi puzzle)[/spoiler]  can be infuriating, as it requires a bit of timing that can lead to some redoing. So head's up.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
I highly recommend [i]Samorost 2[/i] if you're already fond of any other Amanita Design game. However, if you've never been introduced to the studio before – aside from [i]Samorost 1[/i] – titles like [i]Botanicula[/i] and [i]Machinarium[/i] may prove for a smoother first ride.

Last but not least, don't forget to keep [i]Samorost 3[/i] in mind after playing this one, as it is certainly one of Amanita's best titles, and a worthy and memorable conclusion to this involving tale.

I genuinely like the art style and premise of the game. What time I did get to spend playing was enjoyable. Despite some clunkiness in the combat movements, I found the game’s take on dodging and weaving around incoming attacks to be rather inspired. The variety of finisher animations often took advantage of the surrounding environment and gave the fights a much more organic element than I am used to.

Unfortunately, the game suffers from an issue of save-game bloat fairly early on. Initially, my autosave files were around 86kb, but they ballooned to over 255mb in size. Researching online, I discovered that this seems to occur when loading an autosave after dying. Many players suggested reverting to an earlier save and manually deleting the oversized autosaves. Regrettably, the game creates one of these massive autosaves immediately following the first encounter with the main antagonist. As a result, each autosave began to lag the game for longer and longer periods of time, culminating in an infinite black screen after going through a door that persisted despite multiple attempts to reload.

The game also randomly crashes to desktop on startup. This was my experience while playing on an RTX 4090. Despite my desire to continue playing, I reluctantly had to request a refund due to these technical issues.

review_text:
Reviewing this game is difficult.
The game is trying really hard to mimic the iconic game mechanics of its superior counter part (Dead Space) while also trying to introduce new elements that I believe slow and sour the experience.

[b] Things I loved about the game [/b]

- Graphics are quite insane in this title
- Ambiance and atmosphere are definitely on par with the OG Deadspace
- Using a prison and abandoned mine colony as the setting is brilliant, and the contrast between each place does make it feel very unique. 
- Sound design did a meticulous job and its ear candy.
- While the story is predictable and very similar to other Sci-Fi stories, it servers it purpose.
- Monster design is cool as well, while not a 1 to 1 copy of this brother, it definitely keeps those body horror elements.
- Tension is good for the most part.
- There are so many great death animation for our main character and the game embraces the gory elements in them.
- The game is fairly polished as of the date of this review, I did not encounter any bugs or crashed. An unexpected surprise
- I felt immersed in the universe for the most part, partially due to the lack of HUD and details.

[b] Things that I disliked: [/b]

- Having to crawl through small or cramped spaces in video games usually server the purpose to move to the next section in order to not have a loading screen. However, in this game it slows down the pace significantly for no reason and there is A LOT of that in the game. You will be crawling or squishing your way through so many corridors, tunnels and air ducts and it creates FAKE tension, you can do anything besides crawl, therefore you know you can not get attacked in the air-vents. There was only 1 instance where it was successful at creating tension and a scare for me.
- The combat / melee system is not as bad as people make it out to be but is not good either. Instead of using strategy you just have to use rhythm, which immediately kills off almost all the tension from encounters. 
- Switching off weapons is odd, they tried to reinvent the wheel here but instead made it unnecessarily complicated to do.
- Healing is VERY slow as well, which is a single shot, it should not be. Its a way they decided to artificially increase difficulty.
- Reusing bosses several times is always been frown upon, unless they become a re-acuring enemy later down the line, this is not the case. They re use the same boss 3 times and honestly it makes the game less exciting.

[b] Things that I HATE: [/b]
- Performance is not good and honestly unless you have a beefy card I would say stay away from the game, even with a 4080 I had top use Lossless scaling since the game does not have any frame generation and the upscaling method does not have DLSS.
- Manual / Auto saving is so bad in this game, even if you save before a specific part, the game will respawn you all the way back to a different checkpoint forcing you to sell your items and perform the upgrades again.
- Changing game graphical settings is a pain, you can not do it in game and you have to back out to the menu to test the settings and change them.

Overall, I do recommend the game for enthusiast of horror and ambiance. However, for the amount of content I Highly suggest to GRAB IT ON SALE. the story is about 8 hours long which is on the short side and some replayabilty features are locked behind a paywall which is an L in my book.

review_text:
Yakuza 5 - The most ambitious game that RGG studio had ever done.

Story
- 5 Arcs. Each arc for each characters, except Haruka shared her arc with Akiyama, and the Final arc.
- You'll start with Kiryu then Saejima, Haruka and Akiyama then Shinada.
- Kiryu arc is pretty much straightforward. He tried to put his past behind, living as a taxi driver in Fukuoka when suddenly problems came to him. Again.
- Saejima arc tells the story when he's back to prison a year after event of Yakuza 4. Then things happened and he's now in Sapporo (the northern land of Japan, close to Russia).
- Haruka arc tells the story about her path to become an Jpop idol and somehow cross path with Akiyama in Sotenbori.
- Shinada arc tells the story about his struggle as a penniless writer who try to put his past about that faithful day 15 years ago, living as a freeloader in Nagoya when he discovered the dark truth.

Gameplay
- Probably the best fighting mechanic of the PS3 era Yakuza.
- A bit grindy. I finished this game in Normal and it's pretty sweaty to fight against bosses.
- Vast selection of minigames and side quest. Kiryu's Taxi driver, Saejima [spoiler]'s hunting the legendary bear[/spoiler], Haruka's activities as a J-idol and some insight into the Japanese entertainment with various cameo from irl and Shinada's battle against his former teammates.
- I'm not sure if Akiyama has one apart from dancing battle (overlapped with Haruka).

Sounds pretty much a good combination between the story and gameplay so what's the catch?
- Well. It's pretty much can be sum up by one sentence, "R1+A" simulator.
- I don't have exact number but I think this game could even surpass GTA V in terms of word count in the script.
- I mean - point at my hrs count - that's what I got even with holding R1+A to skip the dialog and skip cutscenes. I already finished this game once in another platform so I didn't miss anything.
- I'm pretty sure that if I play the game without skipping the dialog or cutscenes, the hrs count when finished the game would be double.

So just dialog simulator is the problem?
- No. The gameplay also dragging and the story writing is pretty much... not as bad as Y4 but dragging.
- They tried to do the same formula by telling the story of each character, build the background then sums that up in Tokyo, Kamurocho.
- The problem is by the time I finished Shinada arc, I don't recall what happened in Kiryu arc, and barely Saejima's, and had to rely on YT for summary. That's how dragging and the amount of sidestories/gameplay in later arc are.

So.. dialog simulator and dragging story?
- Another thing is that this game is grindy.
- For example, if you're playing on Hard or Legend difficulty I think you probably have to grind for a Tiger drop for both Kiryu and Saejima in the underground colossium.
- I didn't do that and I spent nearly 20 mins to fight against the boss with Kiryu, which could be just 5 mins or 10mins tops if I have tiger drop.
- Saejima also need to grind for his 3rd heavy attack to play this game a lot easier.
- While Haruka doesn't need that much of grinding, it would be nearly impossible to continue her main story without doing the side stories/tasks.
- Shinada is pretty much tragic. If you don't have any interest in baseball or his past (like me), his fight in the final arc is pretty much a nightmare. I finished his fight with health bar flashing.

... Akiyama?
- The problem with Akiyama is simple. "Why did Akiyama have to be in this game?".
- His story is ridiculously short, like 2-3 chapters and it shared with Haruka.
- And the writing is so damn bad like they just offed one significant character just for him to be there.
- I mean it'll be soooo much better if they didn't off that one character. Nobody cares about the characters that sprout from his arc.
- He had to be there just to get that final ending scene. But I don't buy it. They put him there just to make sure he's not the one off character like Tanimura in Y4.

Overall.
It's a good game but it's one of those game that "you finished once and never want to play again".
It's not  because of how bad the combat was like Yakuza 3.
It's not because of how empty the NG+ was like Yakuza 4.
It's just ... nobody wants to play another 30-40 hrs of dialogue simulator, grinding festival and a mediocre story.

And that's so unfortunate. Because this game is probably the most ambitious game RGG has ever done since. 
They dare to put 5 cities from Fukuoka, Sapporo, Osaka, Nagoya and Tokyo in one game. 5 biggest city in Japan. 
And we probably won't get anything like this again. Ever.

review_text:
Like Kingdom Come: Deliverance, the sequel suffers from the same issues as the first game. Wonky and unreliable lock-on, a bad stealth system, bugs and above all the saving system. 

I want to have fun when playing games instead of running around the map looking for herbs just to be able to brew Saving Schnapps to save the game when I want to. Being able to have fun should be above realism at all times and having to put in work to be able to save the game whenever you like is not the way to go.

I will give credit where it is due. They did a great job with the cast of characters, such as Zizka, Godwin, Dry Devil, Adder and so on. The cutscenes were great and they were weaved well into missions.

The game itself is surprisingly well optimized and I never experienced any lag and remained at a smooth 144 FPS at high settings throughout my entire playthrough.

The world looks very nice, the loading screen artwork is amazing and the locations are memorable, such as Trosky castle and Kuttenberg.

Towards the end of my playthrough I encountered a bug that made my character invincible and I could not find a solution for the issue and it did not go away until the very last bit of the story at the siege of Sochdol. Understandably this made combat unbelieveably easy and I didn't even have to abuse Masterstrike. I was even able to slaughter everyone at Von Aulitz's camp outside Sochdol. Obviously this made everything boring as nothing could harm me.

Honestly, the story could of been better but damn, these developers do know how to cook up the worst saving system and lock-on system ever.

review_text:
I am writing this review upon my third playthrough of this game - I can't believe I put myself through the torture of the console version twice before playing it on PC. The PC version is a massive improvement from console in regards to optimization, graphics, and bugs. If you've been hesitant to buy the PC version after playing on console - don't be. It is absolutely worth it to experience this masterpiece as intended.

This is one of the most unique experiences gaming has to offer. Similar to that of Russian literature, this story involves one of the most tragically beautiful blend of spiritual themes and philosophies I've seen in a video game. The developers use of Eurasian folklore brings attention to a topic that I feel isn't widely discussed, and I really appreciate that. 

Pathologic 2 is an anti-power fantasy where the main character... really isn't even the main character once you dig in and peel back the layers. Your choices in this game can reveal a lot about yourself while drawing lines between surgeon Artemy's history and the secrets of his small Steppe hometown of Gorkhon. While the RPG elements are fairly linear regarding dialogue, this game emphasizes that you can't do everything and you can't save everyone, offering you only your free will to complete the tasks that are important to you with time as your only limitation. A fascinating thing about this game's mechanics is that time will always move forward. No matter what you're doing, whether you're working the hospital, talking to townsfolk, playing hide and seek with the local orphans or sleeping, things will happen and the opportunity to interact with these things will pass - much like in real life. When you aren't engaged in conversation you will run around frantically at times scavenging to collect supplies, running from person to person to perform your doctoral duties while also maintaining your own health needs, running from thugs... or towards them if you prefer to fight head on, crafting folk medicine, and managing your sparse inventory space.

The design of this game is one of my favorite aspects, especially regarding environment. A big difference I have noticed between experiencing this on console and PC is how detailed the weather can be and how that can change the mood of the day in game. As you move deeper into the pandemic, the weather has a tendency to get foggier, rainier, and darker, whereas at the beginning of the game you bask in much more sunlight. The architectural elements of this game is also interesting, and plays a huge role in explaining the town's history. As a survival horror/dark fantasy game, you will find some of the most intimidating parts of the map to actually end up being the safest, forcing you to accept and even seek comfort in the dark.

Knowing how few people complete this game based on achievement history across platforms with a massive drop off after the plague hits, I'd like to add this to the discussion: I'm not going to pretend this game is easy in gameplay or easy to get through with it's heavy themes. It's not. It's quite frustrating at times and incredibly challenging and honestly sometimes really uncomfortable to sit through. If you're reading this and have avoided playing this game because of the potential for frustration - don't!! Experiencing this game is so rewarding and failure is part of the experience (and even leads to unlocking new bits of lore at times!!) 

All in all, this is one of my favorite games of all time and I wish I could see this series get more traction. Thank you, devs, for this work of art.

review_text:
[h1] My strategy was brilliant and my execution brilliantly flawed... [/h1]

This is impressively well crafted tactics games as all games from Mimimi games but this one with a flavor of Edo period Japan. With a well thought out plan and buckets of patience you will master 5  agents of shogunate and fight the uprising against imperial rule.

[h2] It's all about puzzles [/h2]

During various campaign missions you will be put into control of 5 characters with unique ability kits. Each mission is essentially treated as a big puzzle but with multiple solutions. At the start you will scout the maps for available routes, hiding spots and tools to help you solve it. You will learn guards' behavior which will open up new paths or give you hints how, when and in what order you eliminate undesirable enemies along the way. Each mission has a specific characters locked in so you cannot choose your team but in that way all missions are built to really utilize the abilities of these characters to full extent.

[h2] Map design is the king. [/h2]

It is indeed the main pillar that makes this game great. The maps are huge with a lot of interesting areas with plentiful options for your agents to work with. And each and every map does its best to feel natural with seemingly no weaknesses until you start looking at them closely. You will notice hidden paths, weak links in enemy routes or interactive objects that could help to disguise your approach or get rid of enemies without raising any significant suspicion. This pairs nicely with your characters’ abilities and makes you consider which sort of approach you are going to take.

[h2] You make the best with what you have. [/h2]

Do you fancy a ninja that strikes from shadows and the rooftops or rather direct approach in the form of samurai capable of disposing of strong enemies or even groups of weaker enemies. How about a seemingly weak girl who can set up deadly traps, or an old 1-legged man with a very deadly rifle. Perhaps a very attractive woman with a knack for disguise. All of these characters have a mix of melee and range options with various advantages and disadvantages. They also possess other utilities to weaken enemies, lure them, distract them. It is only up to you how you use them.

[h2] Oh shogun, my master... [/h2]

The story is rather simple with predictable events but it sits well with how the game is built and played. Characters are likable enough and missions are varied and well thought out. You will conduct your operations in the cities with luxurious residences and busy streets. In wilderness, on the mountain top temples and in the peasant villages. Anywhere your shogun needs you. And all in modest yet beautiful aesthetics and music that adds so much flavor.

[h1] In conclusion: [/h1]

This game is very much captivating until its final mission. But it requires a lot of patience from its player. Sometimes you miss your window and will have to wait for that guard to get back into position or you botch an execution and will have to do the whole set up again. This takes time and quite a lot of down time so if you cannot stand this, pass on the game. But if you do not mind it, in fact you take pleasure in it and you do it right, you set up your characters in a synchronous dance of death where they take out multiple enemies at once without anyone noticing. It is indeed ever so satisfying to see your plan going smoothly.

review_text:
VR Game of the year? 

https://youtu.be/trdiu5tfWGY

Possibly based on the amount of content available and the post game support but like I said I have faith in Vertigo adding in plenty of DLC and Season 1 is included in the price of the game. 

Interested in the story so far. I do wish there was a bit more of it strung together but this isn't a story heavy genre so I'll take what I can get.

The NPC dialogs are interesting but I hope they don't get repetitive. We heard about the old mans date back to back on Chinatown. If I hear that dialog every single run, it's really going to grate on my nerves. That being said, the voice acting is really good. There's some lip flap that doesn't quite line up if you're looking for it but it's far from a major issue.

Visually the game is amazing. Comparable or better to Alyx. There's a nice variety of enemy appearances and as we saw at the end, higher difficulties offer even more variants. I believe I've seen 3 special zombie types at the moment and they're certainly miniboss title worthy opponents. Especially the grabber police a--hole. The Smasher makes for a great boss while also getting hounded by hoards of other Snowies. Environments felt large and lived in. Felt like we were really in the midst of some post apocalyptic town. I loved the mix of interior and exterior environments. My one concern here is that there are only 5 maps atm if I remember correctly. That could get repetitive quick but I expect it will take a decent number of hours to work up through 4 difficulty levels across all 5 maps. At about an hour per run, that's 20 hours to hit all maps on all difficulties. Well worth the price IMO. You'll also more than likely need to grind a little bit for gear or floppies and no one is going to play a perfect no failure game so that 20 is a minimum.

The available comfort options and options across the board are exceptional. Very happy to see this becoming more standard with AAA titles. The one critique here is that I don't think the game ever told you how to open the menu. I randomly discovered it. In a social game it seems very necessary to show the player how to invite and accept invites from players.

Speaking of players I loved the lobby. Everyone was silenced which was golden, but you could see others running around and going about their business. It was an unexpected and nice touch.

The crafting system is neat. Doesn't seem very deep but I like the ability to customize and dangling loot in front of my face will almost always work...

I have very little in the way of negatives to bring up about the game that aren't just potential fears about content or incredibly trivial. Population isn't a concern as the AI isn't terrible. This is what I expect from an experienced VR dev. Great work guys. 100% recommended. Pick this up ASAP. This is going to be a blast with a group of friends.

review_text:
Game is half-finished with a fair number of mechanics feeling very poorly implemented while removing too much of the original to be worth playing this over it.
Treatment of infection is expanded on but ultimately pointless as very few NPCs are worth the investment of tinctures let alone treatment meds. It takes ~three tinctures to find what to prescribe assuming you don't save scum (which the game somewhat tells you to do) which is enough to restore the PCs immunity bar almost fully. This makes the entire system feels more and more pointless as 2/3rds of the characters do less as the game proceeds, something the original justified with the three protagonists.
Thirst and stamina are terrible additions. Thirst is a non-threat but constant annoyance, and with water barrels/bottles littering the map the only way you reach higher than 50% is lack of care. Stamina somehow makes movement across town even more tedious than the original and makes combat difficult to lose in 1v1s.
Death system is a big issue for a lot but I liked it. Until the dozenth or so death, which occasionally causes valuable organs used for tinctures to appear as far less valuable misc items, reducing the usefulness of another kinda new mechanic and punishing the player in a way that isn't nearly in line with the other punishments.
It's a lot easier to pick up what with the difficulty setting and controller friendly but even then the game is so gutted and with the new mechanics feeling so hollow, idk why you'd pick this version over Pathologic HD.

review_text:
I've played this game for years and its fun. Its not the best game out there I don't even know if its qualifies as the best Star trek game but it does offer a good variety of freedom to create a character in the setting. Its the sheer amount of ships, costumes, weapons, missions and other gear is great. You can basically make any humanoid alien you want or play as a standard Star trek race like a vulcan or Klingon. This applies to your crew as well with you being able to customize your bridge crew including thier appearance, species, and uniform. 

Ships are where this game really shines though. A simply massive number of them many with custom traits and consoles that can be transfered to other ships. This can be anything from your standard federation saucer and klingon bird of prey to enigmatic alien vessels like the jellyfish from Farpoint. The only thing I do not like about the ship system is lockbox ships. These ships require you to open lockboxes which are just lootboxes and are CHARACTER bound. This means even if you get a lockbox ship on one character you do not have access to it on any others unless you buy it again. This does not apply to most other ships such as Zen store ships which require you to spend the premium currency and unlock account wide. Event ships are also account wide and feature some very unique and fun designs. Luckily in recent years they introduced Event campagins so even as a F2P player you can get the lockbox ships on at least one character without farming as absurd amount of Dilithium or EC. 

That brings me to the next virtue this game has. The exchange. Almost anything can be traded on the exchange. This includes lockbox ships provided they haven't been opened and claimed. This provides one of the only ways to get lockbox ships for F2P players. In addition event currency for the winter and summer events can be bought or sold on the exchange as well as certain unique weapons, consoles, even bridge crew. 

Space combat is 100% the more fun and focused of the two gameplay modes, the other being ground combat. The space combat just feels more polished and fluid than ground combat which tends to be rather stiff but it does have some fun moments. Its very satisfying to open up a broadside of phasers on an enemy ship or launch a full spread of torpedoes at a cluster of enemy ships. I esspecially love some console abilities which let you make crazy hazards in space like gravity wells, tears in reality, encase your enemies in energy webs or even shoot giant lasers from the front like some sort of super weapon.

review_text:
I had rather low expectation about this but it still ended up being worse than I thought. It is actually a pretty bad and underdeveloped game.

The only good thing about Scorn is of course visuals and while I agree that visually game is pretty creative and unique it gets partially negated by a poor level design. Levels look extremely repetitive with the same corridors and the same circular rooms being everywhere. Game jumps from astonishingly beautifull landscapes to boring copy-pasted locations that become annoying pretty fast.

Everything in Scorn that is not Visuals is just horrible.

Sound design is nonexistent, there is literally no sounds and no music besides some boring ambient on the background.

"Open world" advertisement is a lie. Game is super linear. All your hopes to explore a dark and twisted world of Scorn will be crushed into endless invisible walls and permanently locked paths. 

Scorn has no story and no lore. I mean no story and no lore at all. If you expect to learn something about this world you gonna get disappointed. The protagonist wakes up in the middle of nowhere and starts doing strange thing for no reason at all. You know, even cheap and trashy indie horrors usually provide some lore through document scattered around or whatever. But Scorn gives you nothing.

Gameplay is mostly walking around and solving puzzles that vary from average to ridiculously stupid like you enter a belly of a gigantic monster (that actually looks pretty cool) and suddenly you are solving a puzzle with a ball moving through a maze like in some old game from 80-s. That looks completely out of place and breaks all the immersion. There is combat but it is super basic, boring and is there for the only reason of wasting your time.

Scorn is clearly underdeveloped. You know that game is underdeveloped heavily when a brand new (and pretty interesting) mechanic gets introduced 5 minutes before the game ends. There clearly was supposed to be more but it is not there. I don't know what happened to the developers but in the current state I only recommend this with a big discount and only if you are really into that type of visuals.

review_text:
[h1]Wake up. Time to die.[/h1]
Straight up, Scorn is not a game for everyone. It just turns out that this is the perfect game for demented sickos like myself.

The only real critique I have of the game is its price and runtime. The game itself is really only about eight hours give or take (I have a few more hours on the GOG version), which makes it extremely difficult to justify the $60.00 AUD price tag. It is also a shame considering the artbook and soundtrack are also fantastic. Definitely only get this game on a steep discount, especially if you are unsure whether or not you will enjoy this kind of a game.

Scorn also runs perfectly on the Steam Deck. I was playing on the maximum graphics settings with AMD FSR set to performance mode. It both looked fantastic and ran increadibly smooth without any issues or bugs. My only recommendation is to play with some really good headphones, since the audio design should not be missed out on. If you have a Steam Deck, and feel like traumatising the person sitting next to you on the bus, then look no further!

The gameplay itself is very simple. Walking through various scenes and locations broken up between the occasional puzzle and combat encounter. The movements and gunplay are very slow, which might turn a few people off. I did not mind this, but only because I am more adjusted to slower paced shooters anyway.

While on the topic, combat is purposefully cumbersome in this way, and I feel this is where the game loses a lot of people. The majority of players I witnessed seem to have the false impression that they have to kill every single enemy they come across, in the process wasting their scarce resources, and then proceed to complain about ‘forced combat encounters’ when in reality you can theoretically get through most of the game without needing to kill anything. 

Aside from a select few that will encourage combat, the majority of smaller enemies will spawn in on ‘patrol’ and then despawn at the end of their route. If you do not want to waste your valuable health and ammunition, you can simply break line-of-sight and wait for the enemies to move on. If you do decide to engage in combat, get a couple of hits in, run behind cover, let them spit their acid at you, and then repeat. It is dead simple once you get the hang of it.

I do appreciate that there is an animation for almost everything your character does, making the world feel very tactile and real. While I do think part of the intrigue of Giger-esque art is the viewer is only left to speculate what mechanical functions these contraptions have, I think Scorn strikes the perfect balance of intractability with these devices, while still keeping the majority of these machines mysterious. While traditionally gameplay to me is the most important aspect of a video game, I approached this game from the perspective of it being an interactive artbook and was not disappointed in the slightest.

Speaking of which, what can be said about the artstyle that has not been already recited thousands, if not millions of times over? It is gruesomely gorgeous! Wearing the inspirations from both H.R. Giger and Zdzisław Beksiński on both its sleeves. Despite the obvious comparisons though, I feel that Scorn does retain its own identity apart from both Giger and Beksiński, and that partially comes from the uniquely strange and esoteric universe the developers have built. In true Giger-esque fashion, you will come across various contraptions, devices, and machines that you can only theorise as to their function. Piles of humanoid and not-so-humanoid bodies clambering up the walls, hinting at some greater struggle, extremely Beksiński-like. In this way, it gives the impression that the developers of Scorn both respect Giger and Beksiński and understand their work, in all its cryptic intrigue.

It is because of this reason, that to me, this is where the real horror of the game is. Naturally, horror is a very subjective concept, what might be scary to me might not phase you in the slightest. This game is a perfect example of this, since to me the true horror comes from the atmosphere, the environment, monolithic structures, and glimpses into atrocity. There is something about the strangely familiar yet completely alien environment that Scorn depicts throughout its runtime that fills me with such a unique feeling of dread and unease, unlike any other horror game has managed to capture before.

While there are a few monster enemies scattered throughout the game, they were not the scary part to me. What was scary was the implications that the world and environmental storytelling convey. The horror that gets to me the most is when there are just enough pieces scattered here and there to get your imagination going and inevitably fill in the blanks between them. An audience’s imagination of what something [i]could[/i] be will always be infinitely more terrifying than any writer, director, or designer could say or show it to be.

This is also true for the story, and the greater lore. There is no dialogue to convey the narrative to the player, no recordings, notes, or documents left behind, which I love. Scorn takes the ‘show, do not tell’ philosophy of storytelling to its most literal, leaving only for speculation into the specifics. This removes the inevitable frustration of bogging down the story with long exposition and endless collectable notes to comb through, and simply just [i]shows[/i] you instead. If you do not understand what you are looking at, good. That is the point! Naturally, this kind of story telling should not be applied to [i]everything[/i], it is perfect for Scorn and the world it depicts.

I only wish we could have seen more of the game, especially the last section of the game that takes place in an entirely new location that is distinctly different from the rest of the architecture prior. One can only pray that an eventual sequel or continuation of Scorn will be greenlit someday. I crave to see more of the horrific lore and witness the rest of this dark world the developers have built.

In summary: Scorn is a short game, so get it on sale. It will not be a game for everyone, but if you are a H.R. Giger or Zdzisław Beksiński fan, you will love it. If you are looking for something completely different, immersive, artsy, and esoteric, you will also love this game. Conversely, you will probably not like this game if you are looking for in-depth combat mechanics, fast-paced gameplay, or an easy-to-understand narrative.

If you are on the fence and buy this game on a discount, simply strap yourself in for the ride and just take your time with it. Look around, drink it all in, absorb the atmosphere and the world around you. I think you will be glad you did!

review_text:
So you wanna manage a hockey team, eh?  

Are you sure you got what it takes kid?  Are you ready to handle prima donna stars whose only concept of negotiation is "Either give me what I want or I'm testing the Free Agent market"?  Can you handle trading away the hotshot you drafted 8 years ago, watched become a perennial all-star and lead you to the Cup but now wants so much money it won't leave your team much left to hire the other players you need?  C'mon - you MADE this guy; who does he think he is? Are you ready to take a risk on a high skill player to try to cinch another deep playoff run but his history of injuries is causing every other team to shun him?  Are you willing to scour the back streets of Japan to find that one last guy you need at a price you can afford?  Do you have the patience to try endless variations of lines and unit tactics until you find the magic formula that works for your team - THIS season  - cause next year will be all different and the tinkering will be required again?

You say yes?  Well, kid, then maybe this game is for you!

Eastside Hockey Manager is easily the best hockey sim I've played.  The amount of options it gives you can sometimes be a bit overwhelming, especially if you like playing under the hood to find that perfect set up.  FAIR WARNING though:  options come at a price.  Not a monetary price, this game offers an extremely fair price for what it delivers.  I'm talking a learning curve price.  If you like sports sims , especially hockey sims, do yourself a favor and buy this game.  Then do yourself an even bigger favor and download the Users Manual:  

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/301120/manuals/2015_Game_Manual.pdf

Trust me on this - do it!   You're welcome.

By now, it is obvious, I like this game.  However, in the interest of fairness in my review, it does have a few warts.  The way screens are laid out stat-wise could be improved.  During a game, the Head Coach will sometimes change a tactic and it is nigh impossible to figure out what he is changing because nothing points it out to you.  Sometimes when you set the status of a player you are about to offer a contract to (in effect telling the player how much your team desires him:  "key player" "core player" "regular player" "hot prospect" etc), the player will refuse to listen to you because he wanted a higher status - but you frequently get no way to change the status you gave him.  I get an annoying error infrequently when reading my mail but it doesn't affect game play at all.

There are a few other minor quibbles, but that is exactly what they are:  minor quibbles.  Every game has a few and none in Eastside Hockey Manager are big enough to create caution or concern. 

Fantasy Draft?   check
I Do Everything GM Mode- Keep Your Filthy Hands Off My Team?  check.
I Just Want to Handle Trades and Financials - You Do the Rest?  check.
Minor Leagues?  check.
Foreign Leagues? check.
Gobs of stats? check.
Ability to set lines, team tactics, unit tactics, individual tactics, dictate who takes face-offs, who shoots in what order in shoot-outs, tell specific players they have a green light to pick fights, allow specific defnsemen to carry the puck and/or join the rush, and much more? check.
Realistic results? check.   (Caveat: some people think defensive players with offensive talents are a but short-changed in terms of goals/assists this version of the game.  My experience is I have had various offensive minded defensemen score between 60-80 points a season.  Perhap,s I am just adjusting their personal tactic settings to best suit their play.) 
Ability to customize to play how you personally want to play?  check.
Fun factor?  check.
Stable?  very.
Great graphics?  Come on - it's a sports management sim, what do you think you're gonna get?  The in game graphics are very easy to follow.

Bottom line?  BUY IT!

Come on; do it already! You're wasting my time, kid - I got a practice to run and the #1 team in the other conference is here tomorrow for a big game.  I gotta go!

review_text:
It is tough to evaluate the Yakuza 3-5 set of games. They are plainly a step back, graphically, mechanically, from the prequel Y0 and remade Kiwami 1/2. This feeling continues into Yakuza 5, which like Yakuza 4 before it is a narrative split with more playable characters than just Kiryu. Unlike 4, where Kiryu was kept in reserve until later, we start with Kiryu here and end up with a plot that involves five different characters in four different cities - including Haruka, Kiryu's (formally adopted? I forget) daughter, who is chasing her dreams of being an idol by getting into street dance battles. Yeah, really.

There were big chunks of the game that actively repulsed me. Saejima's portion of the game, which is spent part in prison, part in a completely imagined version of a city, part in the snowy wilderness, and part in the actual version of that city, is particularly bad in this regard. I might have fought two tigers in Kiwami 2 but I'm not here to hunt bears in the snow, with traps and rifles and all that stuff. Haruka's part of the game, while narratively important, is also quite a jarring shift and while I didn't mind the departure, it's also a long interruption from the big yakuza plot that's been brewing now for two games. 4 was an interesting shakeup to the formula but this continuation of 4 was not a good follow-up to that shakeup. There were parts that I really enjoyed but overall... eh.

My gorgeous girlfriend told me Asuna in this  game is Different! She promised to wear a jaw-dropping Asuna cosplay for the occasion. It’s going to be the best cosplay I’ve ever seen at home! Help me out, this is literally my dream coming true. I can’t stop thinking about Asuna 😍.

Unfortunately, I recently had a falling out with my girlfriend because my motorcycle tire blew out and I couldn’t give her time. She got upset and asked, “Who’s more important, me or the new Sword Art Online game?” She doesn’t understand how long I’ve been waiting for this moment, counting every second! Just help me get that 69 award, and all will be good.

Will we really get to live through the first part of the anime series? I seriously hope so. I’m feeling so many things right now, and I don’t even know what to say, but I will say this: I’m beyond excited!

Fighting with a full team is such an adrenaline rush for me. This is my absolute favorite game—Sword Art Online: Fractured Dream. If you think I’m just another casual fan of the game, world, or anime, go take a look at my profile. I’m completely hooked.

I’m really looking forward to playing this with my girlfriend and friends. At last, I can experience the world in a more immersive way, something I haven’t found in VR yet. I’m really hoping this game develops into VR because that’s my ultimate dream—to experience Sword Art Online for real.

My favorite installment so far has been Sword Art Online: Hollow Realization Deluxe Edition. I’ve spent 2000 hours in that game and never got bored. I really hope Fractured Dream offers the same level of depth, missions, expansive world, and gameplay mechanics. More than anything, I want to see Asuna take center stage in this game. I firmly believe Asuna should be the leading character, not just the one always shouting, "Kirito-kun!"

There will definitely be an update to this review soon, I promise.

I can’t wait to see Asuna in this game. Will she be wearing pink underwear on the bed? I guess we’ll have to wait and find out!

First review update: I’ve had the chance to try the beta, and it’s truly mind-blowing. The combat feels like stepping into another dimension, almost like the anime itself. review_text:
After 15.8 hours I have completed my playthrough of Cronos The New Dawn and I must say, this game surprised me! I had an amazing adventure through the world of Cronos that was filled with a bunch of pros and cons, so lets go over them.

PROS:

Graphics - Cronos is gorgeous. Literally, every aspect of this game is incredible looking. From the locations, to the enemies, to the player characters and NPC's, everything is highly detailed, fits the world and is truly fantastic to look at. I kept taking screenshots as I was playing through the game because I couldn't believe how good it looked. 

Level Design - This game features fantastic level design. Truly so much to explore, shortcuts to find, vertical leveling with the gravity boots, it has it all. As you explore the areas and find secret rooms, collectibles (theres alot) etc, multiple weapons. Truly great design.

Sound Design - This game features fantastic sound design which is extremely neccessary for a horror game. The simple yet detailed sounds that keep you on edge as you explore the world are fantastic. The music is great as well (think stranger things style music) and overall its done beautifully.

Gameplay - Cronos features fantastic gameplay. It truly brings survival horror to the forefront. This is not an action game in the slightest. It has moments where it can "feel" action, but you are barely given any ammo, have limited weaponry and must strategize almost every encounter. The enemies who are living will absorb other enemies who are dead or killed turning them into super enemies if you allow them to, so you must always be on edge. A great upgrade system for your weapons and suit, similiar to dead space. Fantastic bosses that are fun and challenging (especially the last two). The enviornment also plays a huge factor in this game and how you approach enemies. Overall the gameplay is solid and I enjoyed it.

Enemy Design - As mentioned in gameplay, Cronos features some pretty fun badass enemies. They are admittingly limited in scope, but thats because they can transform if you dont play effectively. Theres enough enemies here in variety to make it super fun without getting dull. 

Weapon Design - The weapons in the game are super fun. They have 2 modes of fire each usually, resulting in different strategies you can use with them. You wont be able to upgrade every weapon in one playthrough, so choose your upgrades wisely. 

Story - Cronos has a very interesting, very ambigious story that will keep you hooked all the way to the end. You can make choices in the game that will effect your outcome, so this is a narrative experience that can be played multiple times for different endings which increases replayability. 

CONS:

Inventory System - So this game is a true survival horror, it has limited inventory, limited resources. Nothing wrong with this at all. Whats wrong is how extreme it goes with it at the start of the game, almost forcing you to choose inventory space upgrade with your suit cores first over anything else. It removes the choice from the player because otherwise, you will be extremely limited. Also, the game has valuables you can sell that you pick up through the world, but you can only sell it at the save areas. The problem with is, by the time you reach the save area, you will probably have had to get rid of the valuable to make space for something more important to your gameplay before reaching the station. It can be pretty dam annoying at the start of the game, almost too annoying. I managed to get through it with relative ease, but I felt like my choices as a player was made for me, instead of the other way around if that makes sense. 

Horrible Turn Speed - So the main character is obviously in a heavy suit of armor, i get this. Shes going to be very slow. The problem is shes extremely slow, even with maximum mouse turn speed, she is turning slower than anything ive ever seen. Even in dead space it was not this bad and I never had to up my mouse turn to max for that game. This game I am at maximum turn and it feels like i didnt change anything. If you are trying to sell the idea of a tanky slow main character fine, but its frustrating as a mouse and keyboard player to feel that level of slowness when you have an option to increase it and it barely does anything. 

The map system - The GPS system in this game tries to be similiar to dead space, but it doesnt give you a blue trajectory line. It actually doesnt give you anything other than the mark at the top of the compass showing you a general direction. The system is pretty bad to be honest, i would rather there be almost no system because it really doesnt help you much in the game. There is no actual map, so i just personally wish they went all in on a no map style game. Regardless, small con. 

Over reliance on horror tropes: So after having played a couple of games from Blooper, i can confidently say they overly rely on jump scares and horror tropes. This game didnt feel scary at all very much. It was super predictable in every aspect of the horror and more so felt like a psychological thriller than anything else. This game and their jump scares is freaking ridiculous. Towards the end they start spamming it and im just sitting here like...dude stop it thats dumb and predictable. Blooper NAILS the setting, the music, the atmosphere but when it comes to the horror, they play it safe, no risks and very little real fear. 

Overall Cronos is still an incredible game and a fun experience that I might want to do one more play through of just to get a little more. I highly recommend it based on the above pros and cons in its current form at the time of the review. 

If you want to see my entire play through of Cronos: The New Dawn you can check out my you tube channel Hypnotic Gaming LIVE.

Thanks for reading.

cronos has a very interesting, very ambigious story that will keep you hooked all the way to the end. you can make choices in the game that will effect your outcome, so this is a narrative experience that can be played multiple times for different endings which increases replayability. cons inventory system - so this game is a true survival horror, it has limited inventory, limited resources. nothing wrong with this at all. whats wrong is how extreme it goes with it at the start of the game, almost forcing you to choose inventory space upgrade with your suit cores first over anything else. it removes the choice from the player because otherwise, you will be extremely limited. also, the game has valuables you can sell that you pick up through the world, but you can only sell it at the save areas. the problem with is, by the time you reach the save area, you will probably have had to get rid of the valuable to make space for something more important to your gameplay before reaching the station. it can be pretty dam annoying at the start of the game, almost too annoying. i managed to get through it with relative ease, but i felt like my choices as a player was made for me, instead of the other way around if that makes sense. horrible turn speed - so the main character is obviously in a heavy suit of armor, i get this. shes going to be very slow. the problem is shes extremely slow, even with maximum mouse turn speed, she is turning slower than anything ive ever seen. even in dead space it was not this bad and i never had to up my mouse turn to max for that game. this game i am at maximum turn and it feels like i didnt change anything. if you are trying to sell the idea of a tanky slow main character fine, but its frustrating as a mouse and keyboard player to feel that level of slowness when you have an option to increase it and it barely does anything. the map system - the gps system in this game tries to be similiar to dead space, but it doesnt give you a blue trajectory line. it actually doesnt give you anything other than the mark at the top of the compass showing you a general direction. the system is pretty bad to be honest, i would rather there be almost no system because it really doesnt help you much in the game. there is no actual map, so i just personally wish they went all in on a no map style game. regardless, small con. over reliance on horror tropes so after having played a couple of games from blooper, i can confidently say they overly rely on jump scares and horror tropes. this game didnt feel scary at all very much. it was super predictable in every aspect of the horror and more so felt like a psychological thriller than anything else. this game and their jump scares is freaking ridiculous. towards the end they start spamming it and im just sitting here like...dude stop it thats dumb and predictable. blooper nails the setting, the music, the atmosphere but when it comes to the horror, they play it safe, no risks and very little real fear. overall cronos is still an incredible game and a fun experience that i might want to do one more play through of just to get a little more. i highly recommend it based on the above pros and cons in its current form at the time of the review. if you want to see my entire play through of cronos the new dawn you can check out my you tube channel hypnotic gaming live. thanks for reading.

review_text:
I really tried to like this game on Survival in its current state which is probably the last state. It is "the way the game is meant to be played", as the description says. Yet, as one of the streamers noted, "the game requires a very strong attention to detail". Moreover, it punishes you when you are not attentive.

Some players like unfair punishment, and this game may be for you if you are one of them. It has a good technical state for an indie game and has a lot of fun mechanics. I get a cursor problem in fullscreen, yet the game can be played in a window to mitigate that. There are pretty visual effects. The price is not steep.

It does not have saves. Bro, in 2024 even Dwarf Fortress has saves.  The game does have an emergency pause. This is not a pause I want for a strategy game. I want to carefully examine the situation without a rush. The game has a customly designed pixel font which is very small and hard to read. I consider all this as a form of punishment.

About gameplay.

Can you just spam your spells? No, the game punishes you with a constant drain of "total faith", and you have to help your villages to maintain it. There were a few other impressive actions you have to learn, I know they exist (based on my total faith), yet I have not discovered them yet. On the other side, you get a massive faith decrease when your villager dies.

Do you think you can get food flow from farms? No, farmers are only good at picking up the wild crops. You have to regrow the crops via magic. The information like this is quite hard to come by. People say, "Just build 10 farms". No, you cannot do that on Survival and get profit.

These two mechanics are the worst because even if you backup your savefile by copying it, you cannot win against constant resource drain. 

There are some other scenarios when a save backup would help. I sent your villagers to build something near the front line. They decide to attack a graveyard instead. A squad of elite enemy units teleports and destroys my villagers. My total faith is 200 after that, I cannot cast most spells, including the food spell. 

The guide says, "to move enemy back build the wall, the line of catapults, the line of fire pits, repeat". I believe this may work. The point is I'm not really interested in repeating this process 10 times to clean the map.

The description says, "Survival has a steep learning curve". No, it does not have a learning curve. You learn to reset the world after each mistake because mistakes are not recoverable. The guides on the game and YouTube walkthroughs are mediocre.

review_text:
I've followed this game for a few years now and it just got worse since I bought into early access.

First of all, the game requires you to kill enemies in quick succession to finish a level, but it doesn't spawn enough of them to do that for SO LONG on the first level that I get tired of it at that point already.

Second, it's supposed to be inspired by Titanfall 2, but in that game you don't get PUNISHED FOR MOVING. Here, enemies perfectly predict where you're going to be if you don't change direction, so instead of parkour, the best strategy is just spamming A,D and jump while staying in the same spot. You can't outrun their aim because it's predictive and you can't outrun bullets because they're very fast.

The enemies have gotten less distinguishable and less fun to fight. The game had an issue where they'd be to easy to fight or skip, but now one is annoying and the other is impossible.

The random level generation isn't what I'd consider good either. It just places platforms around - you're never locked into rooms that would force you to play a certain way, there's no variety, pickups aren't distributed in a way that makes sense, enemies only seem to spawn as you play so you're never clearing out any area, just wasting time without making progress if you're not charging the exit door with kills.

The combat system is bloated already. Why do we need to have 2 items, an ultimate ability, some kind of special weapon and bullet time? Good movement that's actually useful in combat is enough to be interesting and fun, everything else just detracts from it and leads to dev time being devoted to additions to combat instead of the core mechanics.

review_text:
“While others have flung word-salad complaints and clumsy rants at this game, I have chosen a higher path, to bury it beneath layers of refined, sharpened criticism, each crafted in a distinct literary style. Why settle for one style of condemnation when a game this disappointing deserves a symphony of scorn?”

Rant Style One:

“Rarely has a digital creation so thoroughly wasted the gift of electricity. This so-called ‘game’ is less a work of entertainment and more an insult to human creativity, a pixelated abomination so devoid of merit that its mere existence feels like a moral offense. Had I not received it freely, I would be demanding not just a refund, but compensation for the irreversible damage done to my time, patience, and faith in the medium. Every second spent with this wretched title was a second clawed away from the joy of existence. To call it ‘garbage’ would be an insult to trash, at least trash holds the possibility of recycling. This? This should be digitally exiled, stricken from every server, and ceremonially deleted with salt scattered over the empty folders to prevent its cursed return.”

Rant Style Two"

“Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis is a breathtaking cathedral of digital art, shame it’s built on a swamp of hollow design and shattered promises. Yes, the graphics gleam; yes, the world looks gorgeous from a distance. But once you step inside, you realize you’ve been lured not into a masterpiece, but into a glittering mausoleum, echoing with the ghosts of better games. Beneath the dazzling veneer lies a suffocating emptiness, where shallow gameplay loops, incoherent systems, and lifeless quests choke out any hope of genuine engagement. It’s a triumph of surface-level polish masking a profound lack of soul. The only joy I found was in closing the game and sparing myself further disappointment. To call it a waste would be generous; it’s a tragedy of squandered potential.”


Rant Style Three (Sarcastic):

“Ah yes, Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis: a shining example of how far we’ve come in game design. Who needs depth, meaningful content, or engaging mechanics when you can just stare slack-jawed at pretty particle effects? Why bother offering substance when the graphics alone can hypnotize the masses into thinking they’re having fun? It’s less a game, more an interactive screensaver. Honestly, I’m just grateful the uninstall button works, because after eleven minutes, I realized the most thrilling part of this experience was saying goodbye.”


Rant Style Four (Mocking):

“New Genesis? More like ‘No Genesis.’ Because clearly, no spark of creativity or originality survived the development process. It’s like watching a perfectly dressed mannequin in a storefront window, impressive at first glance, but lifeless and hollow when you get closer. The game tries so hard to convince you it’s something special: ‘Look at me! Look how pretty I am!’ Meanwhile, the gameplay stands in the corner drooling, mumbling incoherently, and tripping over its own shoelaces. The only ‘new’ thing here is how efficiently it wastes your time.”

Rant Style Five (Shakespearean):

“Oh wretched spawn of silicon and squandered ambition! Thou art but a gilded husk, all glitter, no grain; all promise, no delivery. I played thee but eleven minutes, and verily, ‘twas eleven too many. Thy artifice beguiles the eye, yet thy heart beats not. A tapestry woven of empty quests, soulless grind, and mechanics as lifeless as a winter’s stone. Would that I could sue the heavens themselves for birthing such a blight upon the gaming realm! Hence, away! Let no honest soul be tempted by thy false charms, lest they too fall victim to thy dazzling deceit.”


I spent more time hating on this game then I did playing. but in the few minutes I played the game it drove me to write these variety of styles for one style was not enough to express my hatred for this game.

“In the end, it is both tragic and hilarious that I invested more passion, effort, and time into crafting these layers of scorn than the developers apparently did into crafting the game itself. For in the span of eleven short minutes, this title did what few others could: it inspired not joy, nor wonder, but the fierce determination to immortalize its failures in words far more elegant than it deserved. I may have played little, but rest assured, I loathed enough for a lifetime.”

-Bad sprite work. I have no problem going back to SNES games, but To The Moon is just lazy.
-Watts is a miserable character. How is someone so emotionally immature and so childish in charge of implanting artificial dreams into dying men and women?
-Watts spends so much time inside Johnny's memories insulting the man, but then he suddenly cares when Eva wants to remove River from Johnny's memories so that Watts and Eva can do the job they're being paid to do?
-Good premise, but the game does nothing special with it.
-Awful dialogue. This is literally some of the worst dialogue I have ever seen in a game. Very rarely has a game's dialogue made me want to quit and I would have done so if To The Moon had been any longer.
-The game goes out of its way to force comic relief be it through hamfisted references to pop culture about kamehamehas or how TOTALLY EPIC it would be if there was a Doctor Who episode where The Doctor moves a piano using the TARDIS or the scientists' insulting each other. It just drags the game down because the game can't decide if it wants to be a poignant and, at times, tragic story or a wacky journey through an old man's memories.
-What little gameplay exists is awful. Scavenge for memory items that the game never elaborates on save for the ones that send you to earlier memories and the puzzles are dull, unengaging, and just a chore to wade through to progress

The music is nice and the story is pretty decent; unfortunately, a visual novel like this can't get by with terrible writing and a decent story.

The game is garbage.

There are some basic tips but the finer details of play you learn the hard way through experiencing defeat giving the game a bit of a learning curve. Once figured out surviving to late game days where the enemies become stronger as you restrict their building area making them significantly more difficult is pretty easy.
From there comes the challenge, most defense tower units are useless even fully upgraded and without a well planned labyrinth for defense you will find even a meager slime can enter your base and begin to ransack all your buildings. Even with hundreds of villagers and plenty of "rangers" to defend your town one monster can just run around killing everyone while destroying everything you have worked toward. The power creep feels incredibly unbalanced even on traditional mode.
The management aspect is a little tedious where sometimes villagers just don't do their prospective job even when there is nothing left for them to do, let me tell you watching a tower sit at 4 rock to complete building/upgrading can be frustrating especially when the building is set to top priority.
That said, Rise to Ruin has a lot of potential for being a consistently updated indie game. The frustration and challenge can feel rewarding while the defeat can be absolutely heart wrenching. If you enjoy games of this genre I would suggest giving it a try, because I believe Rise to Ruins will only get better with time. For the price of the game you will get your money's worth.

review_text:
Once more evidence that we need a "meh" option rather than just recommend/dont.

GTTOD is fun, it has it's own visual style that should age well and it has decent gameplay loop but.. for 20 bucks there isn't much. Before I rant a bit, I'll just say game good but there's a lot of fixable gripes right now. 

So now for bullet list of those gripes.

There's only a handful of levels and this is apparently the update before 1.0, even if he did add another "act" of levels, the game would be incredibly short and still not worth 20 bucks.

There's only 2 real bosses and they're both melee focused with some ranged attacks, in a game where you're effectively a ninja monkey on 12 experimental enhancer drugs and that's without the upgrades. Yeah dev didn't think boss design that well.

Movement feels great as if you can speed and soar into the air, but the design of the levels seems to want to keep me to the ground. Yeah there are wall run spots everywhere but nothing screams verticality, anything that has a whimper of it fails to keep it consistent and the enemy ai..

The AI is simplistic completely. They just walk at you and do X attack. Some (IMP) try to do a unique position spot so they can spam ranged at you but a majority just walk at you even when they're range based. 

In addition the maps have MANY zones where the player can just be safe, regen shields and even throw grenades/c4 down at the enemy to wipe them. If the player wants to cheese the game it's incredibly easy to, even the bosses aren't immune to this.

The challenge area, abyss or whatever, is completely pointless beyond farming. There is no way to escape it that at least I could find, it's endless dropping that is completely disconnected from the main game's setup so.. why does it exist? It's not actually challenging, you're just dropped into a arena and kill a bunch of guys to get a reward. Since you can't return there's no reason to go into it on a normal run, its purely just to farm and for a rogue game that's... bad imo. The main game should facilitate said farm, not some side area. If anything it just further tells me that this Rogue-like aspect of it was tacked on.

There are many small tiny issues concerning sound design and animation, for instance many inspect animations do not have sounds yet and/or are very VERY basic animations while others have a full visual flare to them. Also inspect animation sounds and camera movement does not stop if you swap off weapon, funny.

The dev, for whatever insane reason that just contributes to the idea that he's just cobbling together ideas, added a fishing minigame. No wonder this game's taking so long to finish.

The game lets you acquire "card packs" from the get go at random, these are supposed to give cards that will, for one time, change your starting equipment. This mechanic is fine and I like the idea. What I don't like is the only way to access this is to level up your character about 3? 4? whole bars in the upgrade tree, which takes awhile since you dont have the challenge area to farm as it's also locked, just to get the guy who lets you use these cards to open. This "shop" should be open either from the get go or when the player finishes the first level up bar of the upgrade system. Not several.

I want to say I like this game, but all these minor gripes add up and the fact that they're touting a 20 dollar front and from what I can tell it was previously 15 bucks for even less content? Is horrible. This game is $10 MAX at current state and unless their fabled 1.0 update adds another 2-3 acts, it should never be above $15 after release.

And the funny thing is, I didn't even pay for it, my friend got me it as a gift, I still feel like it was overpriced. When 1.0 drops I'll check it out and redo the review, for now this is what I have to say : Get it on discount, and I mean a GOOD discount. UNLESS 

IMPORTANT Edit : As one small thing, despite my gripes with the CURRENT pricetag for the CURRENT content. The dev could use the money, if you feel the game deserves the money regardless, fuckit pay full price. After actually checking their discord and talking with the dev myself they seem like they actually do want to keep making the game better and better and I hope they can achieve that.

I hope they keep updating this for a long time.

review_text:
My feelings on this are kinda complicated. On one hand, the basegame is deeply flawed. On the other, there's a fuckton of really good modded content.

To get the main grudge out of the way, the campaign sucks. Simultaneously far too short yet bloated to levels that would make Ubisoft blush. The big core selling point is also locked to like the final level of the game (home doesn't count, it's like three fights and sad music). Levels vary wildly and comically in quality and length, some are really damn fun while others end themselves in a few minutes tops. The good parts are the OST, the fact it only takes about four hours, and how easy it is to just download a dev-save or cheat mod and skip it all.

For positives, this is VR Gmod (even though Gmod has a VR-compatability mod, although it kinda sucks). Runs off Unity which is like fifteen geriatric shareholders and a repressed-homosexual puppyboy away from being open source at this point. Also helps that this game's running on some really potent shit, runs like a dream while holding one of the best physics engines in the business. All that means you get a lot of everything. R2 for codemods like Melonloader and Bonelib so stuff actually works, and Mod.io for your avatars, custom levels and gunporn. If it exists, there's probably a mod for it. Hell the side of the bodymall dares you to find a catgirl model. Main con is that the mod.io integration fucking sucks, a billion times easier and faster to just download the stuff and manually unzip and stick it in appdata (pro gamer tip: locallow).

Game also feels just plain fun to run. The way your avatar moves perfectly in-sync with your IRL body and how every joint and bone is factored in lead to a really immersive experience only comparable to this game's prequel. The bodymod and avatar system lets you make your own fun with challenge runs, seeing how far you can go as a fatass or twink in levels absolutely not built around either, the most fun I had in the campaign was propstacking and using a sledgehammer as a hook to get over a turntable as a morbidly obese furry. The way they pair with the marrow1 system makes every avatar feel distinct, having to learn your height and how you move and eventually figuring out how to control this new vessel just as well as the basic peasant you start with. There's also stat benefits, some avatars run faster or throw things further or can tank more hits, yet those usually come at the cost of size and unwieldiness, sure you may be ten feet tall and bulletproof but good luck reloading a handgun, sure you may be fast and a pain to hit but guns are a lot bigger than what you're used to.

In conclusion, this game's like a raw chicken breast. At base it's horrid and tough to stomach, but give it a nice sear and a lovely spice rub and it's now a five-star meal. Hell, a cabal of madmen ported over the entirety of Boneworks into this game, have your cake and eat it too.

review_text:
I'm going to try and be thorough here. I read some of the magazine reviews - and despite the middling scores from some decided to take a chance and buy it. I had been watching it for a while.

Boy am I glad I did. Some things that have been pointed out - it does have influences from resident evil / dead space etc. But I believe it does a decent job with these. Exploration and inventory management is more like Resident Evil 2 remake... explore, battle, restock; but combat closer to Resident Evil 4 remake. The setting / Sci-fi is where the Dead space influence comes from.

But make no mistake - It is very much its own game. I think they have done a fantastic job for an original IP. Sound design is absolutely top notch. Music shifts as the situation does. The sounds make certain "creatures" easily identifiable... and can create nervous energy.

Graphically - it is a beautiful game, and exploring and alt-timeline post pandemic 1980's Poland is incredible. The creature designs are cool enough - not silent Hill or Dead space remake levels - but good enough. The merge mechanic is an interesting nuance. Some online magazines bemoaned the combat - I found it wasn't as bad as they made out. Sure you get a couple - ambushy type - oh it's a horde... but nothing too hectic. Much like Dead Space Original and Remake - If you don't miss - you will have spare ammo. You can store this in your stash to force the game to spawn more ammo for you and quickly work up reserves. Which you can then sell to upgrade your weapons for more damage per shot and tighter accuracy. It even shares the "health upgrade on suit" fully heals you mechanic if you really struggling...

But what is Really AMAZINGLY cool is the paradoxes created by the use of time travel - and how they affect the story. You actually need to finish the game, and then immediately start new game + on hard. This does two thing : ups the challenge and forces you to use more of the weapons as their dmg potentials are higher than the starting weapons, and two - shows you the true story / ending whilst essentially making - the new game+ - concept a part of the story as part of a time loop. FLIPPING Brilliant! And the best justification for a new game plus mode in a game ever...

It's a really good attempt at a new I.P.  I give it a solid 82% unbiased or 89% because I love these types of games.

The AI will stand there and get smacked by one enemy until they die, and they never shoot the boss enemies where they need to on purpose(Bosses have weakpoints you have to shoot). They never get distance from the enemies, they never stop shooting to avoid damage, or use items like grenades at all nor can you give them items to carry.
So, loads of fun with other players, but loads of frustration and lack of progress running solo.

This game is pretty fun but makes numerous terrible design choices that doesn't bode well for its longevity. I really want to say this is a game that I'd TRULY recommend but it's honestly not. - Combat is pretty fun and responsive.
- The character creator is extremely deep and liberal with what you can do.
- Graphics aren't "amazing" but they're okay

The issue is that the endgame is lacking as well. Skipping the story and leveling up is basically crippling yourself of what little enjoyable content you can get from the game.
