I really wanted to like this game, but I can't help but feel it was misrepresented on the store page.

The trailer does not do a good job of presenting how the combat actually is.   At first, I thought it was just me, but the "fastest" are still incredibility slow.  I got the kitchen knife weapon and it was going the speed I would expect of the long sword.  All weapons need to be sped up by a level.  For example, give the speed of fastest to fast.

I know it's the "design" and that the game wants the player to manage their resources.  However,  having to open the inventory every 10 seconds is rough.  It feels really bad.  Especially when it's what you'll be doing most of the time.

Also, no one should call this game a "hack and slash."  After all, the design of the game punishes that approach.  This is NOT a hack and slash.  You will die if you treat it like one.  

The store page may say "Slash away at enemies," but this is not what you will be doing.  Using "side-scrolling survival action game" is also a bit ridiculous since that describes every 2D game with a health bar.   
My opinion would be improved if the store page didn't use phrases like those.

The resource management of the game's combat needs to be front and center.  
The trailer should also show a minute of unbroken combat gameplay.  Meaning no cuts, not flashy video transitions.  Also with HUD displaying so the viewer can see the resource management taking place.

That or a demo should be available.  Honestly if there was a demo, I think it would nullify any of my complaints.

****More Recent Update****
Can't play this game any more because I don't have the budget for controllers. It's fun, but the random falls drive me insane. The bulldozer AI are annoying as well. Nothing like getting plowed on the holeshot and then falling/getting plowed down 14 times in a race that you just won by 11+ seconds in the first moto. 



***Update***
After playing for awhile, the game isn't as bad as I originally thought. The jumps do seem to be bigger and harder to clear (at least on 250 four strokes, haven't tried 450 yet). It seems the handling could be improved because there isn't a clear area where you might crash. It feels like once you hit that value, you crash not matter what you try. The whips and scrubs are atrocious. The AI is harder as is the whole game. In MXGP 3, I could give a 30 second lead and win a 5 lap race with a decent lead. I don't see that happening in this game for awhile. I'll leave the recommendation as a no, but only because there's not enough new stuff to merit paying the current price. And Matterly Basin is missing...I thought that would be included since it was the Des Nations track last year.

**Original Review Below**


My frustration level has gone through the roof with this game. I was able to get the stuttering to end by turning off anti-aliasing and v-sync...and lowering my settings. This despite an i7 and 8GB 1070...not a huge deal though, but annoying. 

The gameplay is frustrating. I don't like to play with rewind, but I feel I have to in this game to at least have a fair advantage. The AI love to bank off of you in turns. It's also frustrating to nearly rear-end an oppenent in several turns, finally pass them, and then get pushed way wide while a line of AI riders pass you. And then that 250 that's getting pulled in the straights magically has 100hp and just does burn outs and whips you sideways in a turn for no reason. I tested the AI BS factor and found that when I went to push one off the side of a jump, it magically hit a benner, flew back into me and I ended up booted off the track while it kept on its merry way. 

The bike physics seem to be a step in the wrong direction. There's no traction on certain tracks with the bike. The throttle sensitivy seems to be like a lot of car racers; too high for a controller. The same rings true with brakes and you can only adjust by "modular" or "aggressive". Whips feel heavy and do not have a good flow. Scrubs do seem to help a little more, but the 3rd person animation is terrible. These aren't a big deal, but don't tout them if you haven't fixed them.  And while I do appreciate that you can't overjump and case the crap out of things without penalty, I do feel there are certain moments that someone would not wreck in real-life. Slowed down and maybe a sore back, sure, but not a huge wipe-out. And I'm critical because Milestone kept going on about realism in their marketing. 

I feel like I've purchased MX vs ATV All Out for a second time this year; high hopes, big disappointment.

review_text:
First things first, this is *not* a point & click game, it's a visual novel (and not a good one). I bought this without paying much attention to reviews because I thoroughly enjoyed the first game. I won't be making that mistake again. They're nothing alike.

Pros:
- Great music. I loved how well it suited the different areas you were in. This is definitely the game's biggest strength.
- Good graphics
- Trying to use Byers the pigeon with various things continues to be entertaining

Cons:
- For the most part it lacks the humour or the first game
- A huge number of achievements that require repeated playthroughs despite adding no value
- Early decisions lock you out of some later achievements
- There's an achievement that *requires* an autoclicker
- The vast majority of the game involves talking to characters; there's very little interaction with the environment or your inventory.
- There's a huge amount of reading in the game, and an equally large number of text/reading related issues:
- Poor font choice. They've used a font with serifs. Serifs improve reading on books/newspapers/etc, but hamper it when reading on a screen. Sans serif fonts should be used for this purpose. I found it very tiring to read.
- For some reason different characters have different ways the text is displayed. Some of this attempts to reflect the way they speak, but many do not. For example, one character uses / instead of l. Anoth3r charact3r's dialogu3 is writt3n lik3 this for appar3nt no r3ason. These changes consistently make reading more tiring and frustrating.
- I found a lot of the dialogue boring, repetitive, or pointless
- A huge amount of infuriating back and forth travel.
- A lot of the 'puzzles' simply involved figuring out which of the dozens of characters on the train can/will advance the story. Once you find the character that's helpful, start at the top and talk to everyone again.
- A lot of trial and error, which can be annoying. This is made worse by a huge number of bad endings that almost seem to discourage trial and error despite it frequently being the only option.
- Due to the above, the best way to play the game is pretty much just to keep using the hint button and doing what it says
- Most of the train section felt like filler. This is a problem considering it makes up about 80% of the game. It should have been a single puzzle in a larger story.
- What passes for story really isn't very interesting, and largely fails to evoke emotion
- Xerfros's constant self deprecation 'I'm an idiot' comments get tired very quickly

Verdict: 2/10

review_text:
[b]Gameplay[/b]
Combat:
For a free-to-play game, the combat system is surprisingly decent, but it doesn’t come close to the depth or challenge of something like Elden Ring. Most boss fights can be beaten by simply standing your ground, timing attacks, and parrying without needing much movement or strategy. I haven’t tried the harder difficulties yet, so maybe they improve the experience, but I personally wish the game had a single fixed difficulty setting (with the exception of a dedicated hardcore mode).

Stealth, puzzles, and side activities:
The game really shines in its variety of side content. Stealth missions, puzzles, and other unique activities are creative and fun, adding a lot more playable hours and making the world feel more alive.

[b]Story[/b]
Side dialogues:
These are often dull and filled with unnecessary lines that don’t add to the lore or the main narrative. The worst part is when the game uses dialogue just to explain gameplay mechanics—there should be simpler, cleaner ways to teach the player without forcing them to read through long, pointless conversations.

Main story:
It can be hard to follow, mainly because the excessive dialogue makes it confusing to figure out what’s actually important. The story lacks strong character development, and many plot points feel predictable.

[b]Interface (UI/UX)[/b]
The interface is overwhelming when you first start. It’s cluttered with too many menus, tabs, and features that could easily be grouped together. All players really need is a clean inventory tab and a simple skill section. I want to play the game—not spend hours digging through menus.

[b]Graphics & Environment[/b]
This is one of the game’s strongest points. The visual quality is very good, and the world is huge and detailed. It’s genuinely impressive that a free-to-play game can deliver such a massive and visually appealing environment.

review_text:
Ok so here is my review for Samorost 2.

[b] Art [/b] Like the other Samorost games Samorost 2 has some amazing art. It is a little more hand drawn looking than 3 whether this is a pro or a con is up to you but I personally enjoy it and it has a nice feel all around. The art is very consistent and really flows from one place to another. Everything has a nice mix of the look of a picture, an abstract world and random items in the everyday world. The only gripe I have about the art is the lack of screen shots. I really wish you could take screen shots in this game and I would really like it if they added that (don’t expect them to because of the platform its running on and the fact that it’s an older game). Although it is really a con I would still totally recommend the game.

[b] Story [/b] The story in this game like in the others is very simple and nice. I doesn’t make you think too hard and there are really no decisions to make. This might not be for some people but it makes the game wonderful to play when you just wana check out and enjoy some free time. There are 2 main objectives of the story or game and each brings you some fun times and is decorated with amazing art and sound not to mention some great puzzles. The game took me around 4 hours to complete with some help and really feels like a treat instead of a grind. 

[b] Sound [/b] The sound is really an excellent feature of this game. It incorporates great and odd voicing and smooth music/sounds. The environment is constantly being noisy and involves and draws you in with interesting and fun sound cues. I highly recommend playing this game with a headset and if you don’t I don’t think you will get the true feel of the game. 

[b] Puzzles [/b] The puzzles are very nice and unlike samorost 3 and have a clear answer based on the environment or plot of the story. This makes the experience much more enjoyable and you will not need a guide to finish the game if you really wana do it by your own wits and cunning :P. I used a guide that I will link in the description. Most of the puzzles are not too easy and not too hard and can take from 5 to 10 minutes depending on the use of a guide. If a guide is used then you can quickly 2 to 3 minutes. I used a guide on most of the harder puzzles and it took me roughly 4 hours to complete.

[b] Feel [/b] You can tell that this is an older and homemade game. It’s not to polished and is a little bit clunky at times. This is where Samorost 3 and Samorost 2 really differ. You can’t free roam as much in this game. This make the world just a little less inviting but doesn’t really effect the gameplay in a negative way. Sometimes you will get stuck in a puzzle and will have to complete it before you can move or back track again. This is somewhat of a double-edged sword and made it easier to complete the game in a quick run. The other edge is that it also makes it less of a joy to free roam in and just enjoying the environment. In all I would prefer the ability to free roam and be able to walk in various places instead of a semi small area. The last thing is that sometimes your lil gnome or whatever he is will not look natural going or exiting a building and seems to get caught on the walls or doors. Although this games mechanics are not as good as its successors it’s still usually very clean and has a noice feel to it. 

[b] Characters [/b] The characters really gave this game its fantastical feel. There are a variety of distinct species and subsets of characters to interact with. Most of them have a purpose and they really give the game its amazing fun and different feel.

[b] Final Takeaway [/b] This is a great game and a must have if you enjoy fun little games with amazing art and a good old calming feel. The puzzles are great for a relaxing time and generate just enough difficulty to make them feel interesting. The music and sounds are crisp and real and it doesn’t feel like any other game (besides the other Amanita Design games). It’s a steal for $5 USD and you can find it for $2.50 USD or under on sale most of the time. I would highly recommend this game before buying Samorost 3 because if you like this then you will also like 3. Below are a few links to videos and guides I found usefully in the game.

review_text:
⭐⭐⭐½ | Scare: 😱😱😱😱😱 | Combat: 💥💥 | Story/Twists:  📜📜📜📜

When a new Bloober games comes out, I will jump on it as close to day 1 as I can. I really enjoyed The Medium and Silent Hill 2 Remake. Cronos delivered for me in some aspects, but failed in some others. 

What I liked: 
* It's horror. Definitely horror. It's so atmospheric and scary. 
* The story is compelling. The lore is really well-delivered through documents and voice recordings. Voice acting is great. 
* Exploration is fun. I like to try to see if I can find all items (while playing blind). This time around it's cats. It's such a relief to hear a sweet miauw instead of a scary boo. 
* The enemies merging is a fun mechanic. It's not as nerve-wrecking towards the middle of the game as it is in the beginning. 
* The music is really creepy and fits the game perfectly. 
* Ultimately, the question the game poses I really liked. The final decision really made me think. I don't know if I went for the best option, but it felt right. 

What I didn't like: 
* There are some cheap "grab this item and get grabbed and hurt by an enemy" moments. 
* It's survival horror alright. I ran out of ammo many times. I'm not a very expert shooter, but I feel I did pretty well. Credits (to buy stuff) are everywhere but ammo and healing not so much. 
* Weapons take up inventory space, so you can't really carry a full loadout.
* No dodge. No quick turn. Just clompy stomping, which makes avoiding enemy attacks really hard.
* There are a few encounters that felt really frustrating to me with the combat limitations the game presents. Overall it was doable, but especially the final boss battle left me shaking. I retried it (only) three times, but it felt frustrating because you'd want your character to be able to do more. 

Overall, I really like that they created a new game with a new story. They built a compelling Soviet Poland, which wasn't necessarily "fun" to explore but it was enticing. I can't wait for Bloober's next game. Even though it wasn't a game of the year for me, I really do enjoy their storytelling.

review_text:
I will finish this game because I love Henry, but I really cannot recommend it if you enjoyed the first one. Granted, it feels the same, plays the same and it's at the same level of immersion and realism. So if that's what you're interested in, go for it.

But, the storyline is nowhere near as flowy and interesting as the first one. It doesn't hit the same. Henry is in a weird place among the nobles. Everything feels annoying. Having to bear Capon for so many hours at the beginning of the game was a complete chore. Opening the map feels terrible because it takes a while to load. The cities, especially Kuttenberg, are almost intraversable, there are walls everywhere. The map is unhelpful most of the time, you have to walk miles to find a door that allows you to get to your destination. And, the main quest feels like an MMORPG, where you unlock a big stage of the storyline and are thrown into some countless hours of "side" main quests.

It lost the magic of being some dude from a small village, thrown in things much bigger than him and that allowed you to touch the ridiculousness of the people that inhabit medieval times. Now you're much more of an errand boy for the nobility.

Plus, if you want to be a scumbag then this game has it in for you. First of all, guard interaction after crimes is bugged AF. It has happened to me many many times that I fight a guard, only for it to surrender and then spiraling me into not being able to deal with the guard, not being able to kill the guard, or bringing me to an endless loading screen if I try to speak to it. Then, if I wanted to rob the entirety of Kuttenberg at night, with NOBODY SEEING ME, walking to the inn to sleep and the morning after I am automatically labelled as a thief????

All in all, I hope you won't, but for me this game has been a chore and I'm only driven by inertia and because I want to see where Henry ends up. But I'm not enjoying it that much. If you think you can do the same, maybe buy it in some years, or during a big sale.

review_text:
Honestly, not that great of an experience despite desperately wanting to like it after having seen it a bunch on YT and the like.

The "roguelite" elements of it are very evidently a complete afterthought and were probably only tossed in in the last quarter of pre-release development. Your campaign protagonist and team start out generally useless, but even upgrading your protag's stats between runs and buying new abilities and this and that just do not feel that impactful. "Upgrades" very seldom feel like they actually do anything of value a lot of the time, especially when the AI doesn't tend to make many mistakes on account of being AI. They will see what you're trying to do and they will make the objectively correct play to counter it without fail, and a lot of the time that boils down to either being designed to have absurd stats in some category to brute force you or an ability that says "You are no longer allowed to play the game", or some mix of those.

The "Princess" team, despite overall being the second easiest team to beat after the Referee team from the end of the first act, is in my experience the absolute worst of the first two acts hands down. You will spend 95% of the game trying to make a play and having some ugly pink fatass FART on you and you just go flying to the other side of the ice, usually into one of their players who will check you. It's really just a reaction speed test to see if you can pass after seeing that FART CLOUD. Are we 10 years old again? Are fart jokes still funny?

Juvenile jokes aside, farting at the very least isn't one of the many AI abilities they aggressively use off cooldown to tell you "I hate you, fuck off and give me that puck. You aren't supposed to be playing", which is in my eyes one of the worst possible design choices they could have made. review_text:
A game that simply doesn't live up to the one it's trying to succeed.

This game is supposed to be the spiritual successor to Dead Space.  We understand that for legal reason it can't be Dead Space so we got Prison Space.

The story is not very good.  It's constantly looking for reasons to send you down the next dangerous corridor by yourself.  There's a person who's actively trying to help you, but can't be with you in person because reasons.  Even the reason you're at the prison in the first place is stupid.

The characters are also not very good.  They're aren't many and they just kinda do things for the sake of the story as opposed to what a reasonable person would do at the time.

I will say the game looks very good.  Two years after release it also runs fairly well on my aging computer.

The upgrade system was interesting.  I did like that, but I did not like how you could only hold six items and multiple of the same item counted as more.  So four health packs takes up four slots.

Combat is annoying.  There's a difference between hard and unfair and on the normal difficulty it feels unfair.  Jacob (I think that's his name) take damage way too quickly and you'll be dead in about three hits.  They chose to focus more on melee combat, which sounds interesting on paper, but to me was not.  Maybe some people would like, to be fair.

I also have no idea how the GRP works.  It's the game equivalent to Dead Space's telekinesis, but it's not unlimited and I never understood what the small dot on the back of my neck meant.  In general the information The Callisto Protocol is trying to give you on screen to read is hard because it's literally on the back of your neck and that's not a big area.

In general, I appreciate the effort and the idea, but the execution wasn't as good as I think it could've been.

This is a review after ~3 hours of playing. For now, I'm really glad I got this in a Humble Monthly, since this obvious copy of Dead Space is absolutely not worth the asking price. Clunky controls, generic setting, bland story, uninspired enemy design, monotonous and boring combat, predictable jumpscares, and to top it all off, AMD sponsorship which means no DLSS, so all of those raytracing options are doing is killing the framerate (I could barely keep to 50-60 FPS on a 4070). 
It's clear that *some* effort went into making the game, and it's far from being outright bad, and can look really pretty at moments, but it's far from being Dead Space, the game it's obviously trying to impersonate.
It's one of those games that really make me wish for a "neutral" recommendation option.

*edit* after four more hours, I've decided to stop playing and simply watch through the story on Youtube. 

Also, just consider this situation:
The game heavily conditioned me to expect jumpscares literally all of the time. I call an elevator down, and aim my shotgun at it, fully expecting an enemy to jump out when it arrives. Sure enough, the door opens, there's an enemy inside, and I shoot it immediately. They forgot to remove the door hitbox, though, so my shot just bounces off thin air, leaving the enemy unharmed. This has to be like, *the* next level of clunky and anticlimactic.

review_text:
First off don't take any review seriously unless they've cleared it since they really have no idea what they're talking about. The first hour of the game doesn't present the entire picture. I cleared this in one go and got the 2nd ending as my first ending. Great game, amazing graphics and lighting effects. The difficulty is a bit inconsistent and sometimes certain later encounters are easier than earlier one but that might simply be due to the number of options you get in the game. Speaking of options, there's tons of loadouts and types of builds (predominantly bleed + hp regen, poison stacking, or glass cannon mage) and it made me switch equipment so often that I wish there were loadout options in the game since I'd be menuing so often. You could be changing gear every time you encounter specific enemies. Either way I had a lot of fun exploring and discovering new ways to reuse existing pieces of gear once new artifacts and equipment became available and allowed older equipment to shine. Speaking of exploration, this game is labeled as a metroidvania and while you can revisit older areas, there's no reason to do so because unlike other metroidvanias you do not unlock any movement or traversal abilities and everything can be obtained with everything the main character comes with. My personal complaint about the game is that magic is too inaccessible until the very end of the game unless you rely heavily on mana regenerating items which requires even more menuing. It's not until halfway though the game until you find your first piece of mana regenerating equipment (much earlier if you want to get the first ending). I also found that money drops way too infrequently (it's actually way too time consuming to "farm" gold) which makes purchasing consumables not worth it at all so you will want to save consumables for later encounters when it gets very difficult to avoid some boss attacks. There's also a sidequest in the game which involves acquiring some magic spells which will cost you a lot of gold so more useful purchases will be placed on the backburner because it'll set you back quite a bit. Some people have complained about the clunky attack animations and I can agree to some extent. Many weapons are considered "fast" but most enemies will frame trap you between their own attack intervals unless you go with "faster" or "fastest" attack speeds. Dropping straight down like a rock while performing a mid air attack is kind of annoying as well. As far as boss encounters go they are all difficult in their own right except for the last boss. Some bosses will destroy you so easily I had to rely on very specific setups in order to beat them asap.

Post game content is also quite good if you want to replay the game. There are a couple extra modes like playing with specific loadouts and even playing as certain bosses which allows for unique game mechanics.

review_text:
I bought this game on sale, and just recently got to it after watching one of the creators dev vlogs. To be honest, there just doesn't seem to be a point in playing beyond the first 40 or so minutes at the moment.

GTTOD plays like a mashup of Risk of Rain/Muck, Doom/BPM, and somewhat, Ghost Runner.

The game has you rush to find the orange door at the end of each level. Once you find the door you must kill enemies to open said door to proceed to the next level. At the start of each level you can start a shrine that will spawn enemies that get progressively harder as you fight, but these enemy kills don't contribute to opening the door until you reach the door and activate it... they are only spawned to offer you a challenge and some money to buy guns or equipment. As a bonus, once you complete the level with the shrine activated you get some sort of randomized "Buff".

It sounds like a fun loop and the whole story idea of "Climbing to the top of a mountain" sounds awesome. But after playing 13 or so levels... that sense of "climbing to the top" just isn't clear. I fought a level 4 sentinel, and several levels later I fought a level 2 sentinel... why is the later enemy weaker? Am I making progress or am I not? The repeating level layouts didn't really help the case, so by that point I figured the game simply never ends because it is in Early access.

While guns, Gun slots, and equipment can be gotten fast enough (and are all mostly satisfying to use)...
Buff accrual is too slow in this game. Games like BPM, Muck, and Risk of Rain all had a pretty decent rate of Buff Accrual since you could pick up buffs from shrines or chests.

As the Early Access would let on, the game isn't ready for release. It needs work and the developer knows and is hilariously vocal about it in his lovely Dev VLogs on steam. I'm keeping this game to support the developer and because I look forward to seeing what this game can become, but my review will not be kept as "recommended" out of hope or pity. It will change to that when the game becomes more fleshed out and progression becomes more apparent.


Minor Notes to DEV:
* Tutorial was appreciated
* Level design is mostly nice... some parts need more clarification on intended direction, some parts feel like there is only one real path to the end. The first level with the wire fence I walked around in circles about 3-4 times before I found the door.
* Add some way to scroll up and down display Settings in case you don't have or use mouse wheel
* Add a window to look at all of your current buffs in detail
* Add a QuickSave option if this is intended to be an endless game without any goal aside from padding stats against the ever strengthening enemy

review_text:
".hack//G.U. Last Recode" is both a terrible name for a video game, and a selection of 4 very badly console ported Playstation games.   The game has you playing the role of someone playing a game that is based on an anime of people playing a video game, so that's un-necessarily meta, and it really doesn't make things better here.   

Gameplay in each of the four games consists of watching cutscenes, skipping cutscenes, and actually playing this third person brawler/JRPG for anywhere up to 30 seconds before the next cutscene triggers, and watching cutscenes.  Some of the cutscenes have cutscenes.   Japanese game developers, please learn how to tell a story through the interactive medium of video games instead of endlessly ramming bad cutscenes down people's throats.  My gaming rig is not a TV set. 

Once you do wade through enough of the cutscenes that you're allowed to play the game, you'll wish you were back watching cutscenes.   This is a tremendously bad console port (why is it always the PS console ports that are the worst?).  The keyboard mappings are quite simply brain damagingly badly done.  "E" apparently is what we normally use backspace or escape for, for example.   Of course there's no proper mouse support, because consoles don't have gaming mice, so screw you PC gamers.  You're basically expected to play this with a console peasant children's toy gamepad, and even then it's a terrible experience, as the camera controls are done using an analogue stick.   It's just garbage tier game design and the developers brilliantly decided not to bother fixing their design flaws when porting to PC.   Bandai Namco would like you all to know that they've never played a game with mouselook before and don't understand why anyone would want such a thing. 

Assuming you've confused this PC edition with a Playstation edition and you're happy with terrible controls, the graphics are terrible too.  While there's 4K support for the game (but not much else in the way of graphics tweaks), the graphics look very 2005, and not at all 2017 when this trash was dumped on Steam.

That doesn't stop Bandai from charging an absolutely comical $70 for this console garbage.   You can get Skyrim for less than $10 for comparison, and that looks better despite being much older than this.  Skyrim's developers managed to work out how to let you look around using the mouse.  So if you want a good RPG, buy Skyrim 7 times.   Or if you like the Hack anime series, go watch that, it's like the cutscenes in this game but not as annoying.

review_text:
Read somewhere that this was originally intended to be a single player game. If that's true, you can definitely see how that could be the case. The solo game play is pretty great, for the most part. The story is interesting enough. The gameplay is pretty fun and exploration/leveling is genuinely rewarding. 

What I hate is that certain injuries require me to deal with other players to get them healed since the NPC healer can't handle certain levels of ailment. So then I get stuck waiting forever to find a player to fix my stuff, unless of course you play with friends (which luckily my boyfriend also plays and takes care of me but before he ranked up healer it was excruciating.) I also feel like they wanted scholar to be as gameplay involved as healer was as far as being multiplayer applied, and I absolutely hate how they integrated it. The jail system is stupid. Other than having the badge of (dis)honor for being jailed for over 160 hours as a joke, this just kills gameplay. (which, what? You want me to be in game jail for a realtime 160 hours for an achievement? fuck you.) You have to get a player to be your lawyer (scholar) and you need in-game bounty tokens to even get them, which makes an already inconvenient feature even more fucking annoying. Not to mention you can just get falsely accused of crimes by NPCs even in solo-mode, and then get your ass beat by a player who's taking in your bounty because you didn't even know there was a bounty board system to hire a fucking lawyer. 

Multiplayer co-op is also genuinely horrendous. About 1/10th of the time were my friends able to actually join me in the heartseeker combat. There was no understandable reason as to why that was. They were the same level as me, same progression rate as me, in my party, in my team, in my guild, in every possible thing you can imagine, and still it wouldn't let them join. They would get locked out of the arena. And to make it more confusing -- sometimes it DID work and let them join the fight. So I legit don't know what arbitrary function was not functioning. And then on top of all of that, it would sometimes glitch out when we WERE able to fight heartseeker together and say we were both still in the dungeon when we left that could only be resolved by going into online mode, then back into solo mode. Nothing else worked, not even leaving the party/team.

A personal complaint of mine, which again is with a grain of salt because I don't even like playing online mode: I went to online mode to do the disciple/partnership ceremonies, and got killed at random by other players. Legit don't even know how. Was in the screen doing my thing, and when I finished setting up the partnership, was just dead. So that was great!

Also, just a petty grievance: SIGN POSTS WERE A PLAGUE. It works in dark souls because it limits the amount of bloodstain messages and doesn't get in the way when you're trying to interact with other things. This game is littered with them so much that I had to just turn them all off in general so it wouldn't bog my shit down.

And aside from my gripes about multiplayer shenanigans: The game is just broken at times. There is a quest at one point where you need to board a warship, and to do so you need to get on a lift. I did that, then fell of the lift because it doesn't keep your character in place while you're riding the fucking thing. So I fell off, and into the water. Was like, whatever no big deal, sure I can call the lift back. Nope. Had to redo the whole quest from the beginning, and honestly didn't even want to at that point.

Combat is weird. Sometimes my Q ability with the spear will lock onto targets and not pop off until I'm in range, or forces me to walk toward a targeted enemy to set off the ability, and then other times it just goes off no problem. Don't know what that's about but it's annoying as fuck. Some stairways are insanely annoying to walk down because your character auto grapples to the banisters in front of you instead of just GOING DOWN. It has driven me to madness on more than one occasion. The wall running is janky as well. I also love having my stamina exhaust because I get caught on a rock that doesn't even make sense getting caught on? I also constantly break my legs and get sprains, even though I always hit my Q to do the safe drop with the bonus to mitigate/remove fall damage. Yay spending 10K coins, because otherwise to "self-heal" you have to just not do anything for an hour in game. 

Also, the puzzles are terribly translated for english speaking users. The first main fortress has a puzzle you legit can't solve unless you understand chinese, as well as at least one of the meow meow puzzles (the lantern puzzle in kaifeng specifically. It's a word puzzle that's just a direct translation and doesn't make sense because they didn't change it to make sense in english.)

The UI is confusing and obtuse, making common functions 4 buttons deep instead of instantly accessible, but don't worry, they'll make sure you have instant access to their cosmetic shop!

OH. AND DON'T EVEN GET ME STARTED ON THE CONSTANT REMINDERS OF THE BATTLE PASS, THE DRAWS, AND THE LIMITED ITEMS. I DONT CARE. LEAVE ME ALONE. 

Also, just for anyone who cares about this type of thing since they don't outright inform you of it: This game uses a lot of AI features, both for some interactive puzzles, and for NPC interactions. I also believe there's a decent chunk of voice acting and art that was AI generated. Which the AI voices really drag down the emotional impact of certain scenes. A flat performance by AI that can't understand emotional subtext is really noticeable. 

It's frustrating, because I actually really like this game. The story is compelling, the gameplay is fun, the loop is addicting. I like the grind and don't feel bored by it. Exploration is genuinely interesting and rewarding. I enjoy the journal grind. I like finding anecdotes and unlocking little hidden side stories. I love the lively world. It feels like there was so much attention to detail there, that it really highlights the areas that are lacking. The character customization is in depth and a lot of fun. I love the wuxia themes, and feel like they implemented them AMAZINGLY. Every single weapon and weapon skillset is fun to play, and has its merits. The customization of your build is endless.

It just feels like it needed another year in the oven to bake. Either a lot less multiplayer, or MORE multiplayer if they're going that route. It's hard not to feel like this is a quick cash grab for some cosmetic bullshit and then they'll forsake the game in a few months from now. The industry standard seems to be that way these days.

I wish there was a mid option, because I don't hate the game. I like the game. I just hate a lot of what it is at present. So until some things are improved, I'm giving it a thumbs down.

After 5 good games, from Yakuza 0 to Yakuza 4, I couldn't finish this one. It's just annoyingly boring and super long.
Yakuza 4 had better plot, but minigames were very shallow and scarce. I really don't understand why did you even need to have Saejima's part here: there's only one or two interesting moments. Baba is really badly written too. He's just lame in everything, including his face.
The only star of originality in this dark space of boringness and self-copying is Haruka's part. Always wanted to play as her. Oh, and taxi driving too.

Overall, if you're an Yakuza fan, just play the main story, and forget about it. For other people not familiar with Yakuza games, I really can't recommend it.

review_text:
Well, it's sad I have to do the review this way, but so far MXGP PRO was a major disappointment for me. They really built up a lot of hype for me with the first announcement, but now we are sitting here with MXGP 4. 
Don't get me wrong, if you like the other MXGP games this game is great aswell and they managed to improve themselves just like with every other MX game they made since MXGP1, but it's not what you would expect with the pro advertisement.

Before I can start with my pro and contra points, I have to mention something that wasn't clear for me and some of my friends.
It's known that there are training missions in the game, but I didn't realize you actually have to do them before you can enjoy the game. They have a major impact on how the bike feels.

negative:
- the game should direct you after or without the tutorial directly to the necessary training missions, but it doesn't
- after doing the missions the bike feels way better, but thats the reason the game became just as easy as all the games before --> first 2 gps without training I struggled to not get last, first gp after the training was a win (pro physics vs realistic ai and ~18 years of playing mx games...)
- terrain deformation looks not that bad, but to feel your rear wheel sliding into a rut is a rare occasion. impact on riding is nearly 0
- whips are way better, but still not what you would expect from the free whip advertisement
- perfomance is disgusting. the steam fps counter shows locked 60 fps, but the game feels like 20-30 maybe and sometimes i have actual small fps drops too with a ok rig
- when changing from window to fullscreen, my game is flickering green all the time until I change back to window mode
- surname only 8 characters. This wasn't a thing in the previous 4 MX games, why tf now?

positive:
- you crash easier now, which was kinda a challenge in the previous game (not that much that the game got hard now...)
- beside the mentioned negative points, the game is a improved MXGP3 which isn't bad
- mid air bike adjustments are finally here

review_text:
I liked KCD 1 and fully expected to enjoy KCD 2 as well. 
30 hrs in with at least that much to go, I can say the game is just not fun. 
I really have to force myself to play.

The game certainly looks good but the story is nowhere as good as KCD1. 
Plus, all the other issues listed below really hurt the game.

Endless cut scenes that sometimes last as long as 5 minutes.

Following NPC's on foot or horseback  just to listen to boring conversations for several minutes which ends with yet another long cut scene.

Combat that hasn't improved or evolved at all from the original KCD.

Mechanics in the game you can't use because it impacts negatively somewhere else.

Examples: 

Want to use fast travel allot, your horsemanship will never improve.

Want to talk your way through things, well prepare for a soft lock when you can't win a battle that advances the story. 

Want to fight allot, prepare to fail all the speech checks because your speech and charisma are to low.

I'm sorry but the game just feels like a slog to play. 
Sometimes, bigger isn't always better.

UPDATE:

After playing another 30 hours to complete the main story, I can tell you it doesn't get any better. 

The cut scenes get longer and longer. I mean their are times you are literally staring at the screen for 10 minutes doing nothing. Maybe this works when you have an interesting story but this story is so boring. 

Also, the last several missions focus on the weakest part of the game. 
You are forced to engage in repetitive battles at one location over and over again. Why?

This game turned out to be a massive disappointment.

review_text:
If someone told me they could only afford one game, Boneworks or Bonelab, I'd tell them to get Boneworks. Boneworks feels much longer, has a better soundtrack, makes more sense with its physic interactions, has better looking enemies, and actually feels like it has some kind of story.

When you play Bonelabs, it feels like you start with a tutorial for the new player models which all have unique features. You get to try out these features with a couple of purpose built levels per model. Then, it feels like you're about to be let loose into the main story or main part of the game, only to find that it's actually the end of the game.
